item.title: Yahoo Fantasy x BreakingT Week 11 shirt: A Mile-High Salute for Jonah Coleman
item.description: Yahoo Fantasy is teaming up with BreakingT to launch the Yahoo Fantasy Shirt of the Week. Yahoo Fantasy is teaming up with BreakingT , home of the fastest-licensed fan gear in the world, to launch the Yahoo Fantasy Shirt of the Week, celebrating the one play or player that defined the fantasy week. The names on your roster are about to be the names on your chest. BreakingT is a newsroom that happens to make shirts. Using its proprietary CrowdBreak platform, BreakingT tracks what fans are reacting to across social media in real time — surfacing the moments, memes and micro-stories that matter most to each fanbase — and its design team turns those moments into officially licensed gear in hours, not months. How it works Every week of the NFL season, once the Monday night game goes final, the Yahoo Fantasy team will crown the play or player that defined the fantasy week. Some weeks it's a single snap — the 75-yard catch-and-run that decides thousands of matchups, or the goal-line plunge that flipped your week with 30 seconds left. Other weeks, it's a full-blown eruption — the four-touchdown, 200-yard game that carried a lineup on its own. Whatever it is, BreakingT turns it into a shirt, and that shirt drops. Every Tuesday. All season long. Missed out on a Yahoo Fantasy x BreakingT drop? You can still purchase any of the weekly shirts here! Now, when the fantasy week resets, you can also pick up gear that celebrates your victory and puts the rest of the league on blast. Week 11's shirt: Jonah Coleman, Mile-High Salute Jonah Coleman went from just another piece in Denver's backfield to looking like a fantasy football league winner in Week 11. The Broncos rookie put together the best game of his career against the Raiders, rushing 24 times for 111 yards and three touchdowns. For those of you in a PPR league, Coleman added four catches as well. Coleman has scored in Denver's past three games and the fourth-round pick looks to have a firm grasp on a role in the Broncos' offense. Jonah Coleman, Mile-High Salute. (BreakingT) Buy your Jonah Coleman, Mile-High Salute shirt now! Fantasy football used to live on your phone. Starting this week, it hangs in your closet, too. With a new shirt every Tuesday built around what actually happened on the field, this is fantasy gear that keeps up with the season in real time — and a collection you can only build one week at a time. Check back every Tuesday, and get ready to wear the moment.

item.title: Ivan Perišić proves age is just a number with latest UCL feat 👨‍🦳
item.description: Ivan Perišić proves age is just a number with latest UCL feat 👨‍🦳 Ivan Perišić is becoming the Champions League's master of pushing boundaries. At 37 years old, the midfielder has become an increasing symbol of seniority in Europe's elite club competition as he continues to rack up numerous records. Already in possession of the title for the most oldest player to score in consecutive knockout matches, Perišić added another accolade in PSV's clash with Real Madrid. The Croatia international stunned the Bernabéu by opening the scoring for the visitors in Tuesday's league phase encounter courtesy of a trademark penalty effort. It means that Perišić is now the oldest player to ever convert a spot kick in the Champions League as well as to net against Los Blancos in the competition. Proof that age really is just a number!

item.title: Barcelona star risks Hansi Flick’s wrath after public training mishap
item.description: Barcelona star risks Hansi Flick’s wrath after public training mishap Barcelona star Jules Koundé has on Tuesday risked the wrath of head coach Hansi Flick. This comes after the Frenchman was a late arrival for an on-pitch team talk. Barca are of course currently in the thick of preparations for a return to action on the continent on Wednesday night. The Blaugrana have made the trip to Azerbaijan’s capital of Baku, ahead of locking horns with minnows Sabah. On Tuesday, Hansi Flick’s squad were put through their paces on the pitch, in a final preparatory session for the fixture. This was followed by a public team talk, also held on the pitch, involving the Catalans’ travelling squad and the entirety of Flick’s staff. As alluded to above, though, with the talk already underway, one member of Barca’s defensive ranks was nowhere to be seen. As per a report from Mundo Deportivo : ‘Koundé joined the team a few seconds late, after they had already lined up, and the coach looked less than pleased as soon as he noticed. Many of his teammates also watched his late arrival with undisguised curiosity.’ This is far from the first occasion on which Koundé has angered his manager with his tardiness over the last couple of seasons, with it now remaining to be seen whether or not the former Sevilla man faces a punishment. Conor Laird – GSFN

item.description: The Blueprint is my weekly column and basically everything that I use to build out the most accurate rankings I can. There will be an RB column , this WR column and a combination column on the onesie positions. You will find film notes and endless charts. Maybe enough charts to stress test the Yahoo website. I kid. It's impossible to get every ranking thoroughly early in the week, so be sure to keep checking in on these columns through Sunday morning. Jaxon Smith-Njigba (at SF) - 97.5 proj. receiving yards Smith-Njigba is the WR2 in per-game half PPR scoring on WR6 expected-points usage over his past four games with Drew Lock and Sam Darnold splitting time. He has topped 100 receiving yards in three of those four contests while drawing a 44% target share in that span. What's new? San Francisco ranks 11th in half PPR points allowed per game to opposing wideouts, having surrendered 71.2 fantasy points to the Cowboys receiver room in Week 10 when chasing points. JSN has tons of experience against this defense, most recently posting 118, 19, 84, 124 and 118 yards. Seattle travels as 3-point road underdogs with a 21.75-point team total (17th). Throwing the ball to the perimeter is the best way to move the ball against the Niners, in my opinion. 3. Through 11 weeks of an NFL season, Lamb's 208.2 half PPR points are 13th all time. All time . The Eagles have been bad against Lamb-type receivers all year and now won't have All Pro LB Zack Baun. As always, my full rankings at every position will be updated here soon . 1. Ja'Marr Chase (vs. NO) - 93.5 proj. receiving yards 2. They've allowed the third-most points to fantasy WRs, and Lamb finished as the WR5 on WR1 overall usage against them in Week 7. Dallas carries a 28-point team total (fourth) as 8.5-point home favorites. 4. Amon-Ra St. Brown (vs. CHI) - 84.5 proj. receiving yards St. Brown is having his usual season. He's the WR5 on WR7 usage, after going on a touchdown-less rut throughout October. This matchup has the potential for a blowup game. The biggest factor will be if slot CB Kyler Gordon can play after he missed last week. The Bears have been pretty woeful in the secondary beyond him, while shutting down the run since Jeffery Simmons appeared. The Sun God was the WR5 and WR1 in matchups against them last year, both wins for Detroit. Jaxon Smith-Njigba hung 118-1 against them in Week 8 in a similar role, too. Detroit enters as 2.5-point home underdogs carrying a 26.5-point implied team total (sixth). 5. Tee Higgins (vs. NO) - 70.5 proj. receiving yards (Photo by Hayden Winks/Yahoo Sports) 6. Parker Washington (vs. TEN) - 78.5 proj. receiving yards That really should've been a touchdown . Come on, refs! Washington still was a top-20 WR last week and is now the WR13 on WR12 usage across the season. He can be up-and-down based on the Jaguars' lopsided history, but when games are tighter, Washington catches fire, as he did last week when he racked up 16 targets while trailing. (Chart by Hayden Winks/Yahoo Sports) This week, the Jaguars are expected to go crazy on offense. They have a league-high 31.0-point team total against the Titans, who have allowed 362 passing yards per game over the past month. Read that again. And again. It's one of the wildest stats of the year. It doesn't take a genius to feel good about Washington's ceiling odds here. He had 152-1 against them just two weeks ago. 7. George Pickens (vs. PHI) - 70.5 proj. receiving yards We're so back. Pickens has 38.0 and 20.3 half PPR points, respectively, in his two games since the bye. He had one of the best grabs of the year last week along the sideline, while Dak Prescott had all day to pass behind a great Cowboys OL. It's an environment for Pickens to have monster games, even if his role and style come with some volatility. He's at his best when teams go to single high coverage, something the Eagles typically don't do. That said, CB1 Quinyon Mitchell is dealing with a new hamstring injury, and the other star players won't be available with Jordan Davis on the Jaguars and LB Zack Baun on IR. Mitchell's status is a big deal for Pickens' matchup. Across the season, the Eagles have had far too many blown coverages, leading to the third-most fantasy points allowed to WRs (31.3). Pickens had 57-1 against them in Week 7 and 146-1 against them late last year. Dallas carries a 28-point team total (fourth) as 8.5-point home favorites. 8. Malik Nabers (at IND) - 64.5 proj. receiving yards Nabers had a handful of underneath receptions against elite CB1 Travis Hunter last week, then teleported into the back of the end zone against Jacksonville’s nickel defender to bring Nabers to a top-15 WR finish. Since Week 4, Nabers is the WR9 on WR4 usage with Puka Nacua as one of the receivers ahead. Things will always be up-and-down with J.J. McCarthy, who missed him way out of bounds for a potential back-shoulder TD, but Nabers is way too good to not be treated as a fantasy WR1 now. (Chart by Hayden Winks/Yahoo Sports) The Giants have a healthy 24.0-point team total this week, and that'll easily be one of their best all year. The Colts are tanking and have allowed the 10th-most passing yards per game over their last four games. We'll see if CB1 Sauce Gardner or CB2 Charvarius Ward will return this week. Nico Collins had an awesome deep touchdown against their backups last week, and Nabers had a 171-2 game against the Colts during his rookie season, for what it's worth. Long story short, Nabers looks great this week. 9. Justin Jefferson (vs. ATL) - 84.5 proj. receiving yards Jefferson is the WR18 on WR8 usage over the past two weeks with Kirk Cousins. The fumble on that in-cut explosion was a real bummer, but that completion had a lot of timing and anticipation from the QB, something Jefferson hasn't had since 2023. He had plenty of breaking routes against the 49ers, and Kevin O'Connell drew up two different downfield shots to him, too. A big game is long overdue. The signs of it happening soon are there. (Chart by Hayden Winks/Yahoo Sports) This is a sweet matchup for just that. The Falcons don't have Pro Bowl FS Jessie Bates, and CB1 A.J. Terrell is having a down season in isolation. The Vikings getting their OL healthy again would be nice, but Jefferson should have room to operate either way. The Falcons have allowed the fifth-most passing yards per game this year and the seventh-most fantasy points to WRs. Minnesota has a strong 24.75-point team total, and Jordan Addison (finger) isn't expected to play. 10. Nico Collins (vs. BAL) - 63.5 proj. receiving yards Collins ranks as the WR18 in half PPR points per game on WR31 expected-points usage across his last four appearances. His weekly target volume has fluctuated wildly, bottoming out at four targets in two separate contests while spiking to 15 targets in Week 10 against Cleveland. The good news is the Texans have recently ramped his snap rates up out of desperation and with Marvin Harrison Jr. and Jaylen Noel sidelined. Collins is the WR11 on WR20 usage this year. That's a fair range for him. A long dunk-on-you TD made him the WR18 last week. Baltimore's defense has underwhelmed. We'll see if podcaster Marlon Humphrey is back this week, but he's been bad this year anyway. Collins will likely see a bunch of CB1 Nate Wiggins, who has the speed to match with Collins downfield. Opponents facing the Ravens have posted a 46% neutral pass rate, the third-lowest rate in the NFL and the Texans are 6.5-point home favorites. He likely won't have that many targets here, but a 26.5-point team total (seventh) suggests he'll be a big reason why that is. 11. Matthew Golden (at LAR) - 74.5 proj. receiving yards Golden has produced as the WR8 in half PPR points per game on WR5 expected-points usage over his last four games. T

item.title: Palo Alto Networks Takes Over La Quinta For New PGA Series
item.description: John (Jack) Power-Imagn Images The desert golf scene in La Quinta is changing fast. American Express will not return as the title sponsor for the 2028 season. This marks the end of a 68-year run for the tournament that helped build the region’s winter sports identity. The shift brings a cybersecurity giant to the scene instead of a financial services firm. It signals a major pivot for the PGA Tour as it launches a new tier of competition. Palo Alto Networks is the new lead sponsor for the event starting in 2028, according to KESQ . The company will take over the title rights after the 2027 tournament finishes its run under the American Express name. The 2027 edition is set for January 21-24, and it will be the last one played under the old deal. According to KESQ, the new tournament name has not been announced yet. The change is part of a broader plan to create a Challenger Series with a fresh format. A New Series for Rising Stars This move creates a specific path for players who need to climb the ranks. The Challenger Series will feature a 20-event schedule with a season-long points system. It is designed to mix established pros with up-and-coming talent in one competitive field. Per KESQ, this structure gives players a clear way to advance within the Tour without waiting for an open spot. Television coverage will be a key part of the new package. The La Quinta stop will be one of seven events in the series to get network television time. This setup ensures fans can watch the action even if they miss the weekend finals. The Tour wants to keep the spotlight on the desert while expanding the reach of the new series. Corporate Shifts and Local Pride The local community has seen this event since 1960 when it started as the Palm Springs Golf Classic. It grew into a major winter attraction that drew crowds and big names every year. Now, the identity of the tournament is evolving with a new corporate backer. Dhruv Prasad, Chief Commercial Officer of the PGA Tour, welcomed Palo Alto Networks as the first lead sponsor for the new series. He noted the importance of partnering with another California-based company to maintain the Tour’s presence in the Coachella Valley. Nikesh Arora, the Chairman and CEO of Palo Alto Networks, stated the company anticipates elevating the tournament experience. He specifically mentioned the players, fans, and amateurs in the popular pro-am competition. The event has a long history in the desert, and the title sponsor is changing. According to KESQ, the event remains one of the PGA Tour’s recognizable stops despite the corporate shuffle.

item.title: Mizzou Football Chemistry Builds Through YAC Success And Trust
item.description: William Purnell-Imagn Images The Tigers just put together one of their strongest offensive shows of the season on Saturday night in Columbia. The wide receiver group racked up 159 yards after the catch, which set a new season high for the team. Head coach Eli Drinkwitz knew exactly what to expect from the opponent. He saw a team that played a loose zone defense and planned to exploit it. The game plan relied on accurate throws and receivers who could move well. That is exactly what the team delivered on the field. Building Trust in the Offseason The connection between the quarterback and his targets is the key to this success. Quarterback Austin Simmons has been working hard to build that bond with his receivers all year. He noted that the team has been practicing specific routes and timing for months. The result was a play where Naeshaun Montgomery made a big dig route look easy. Simmons said, “We have guys that can make plays, especially in big time moments like Naeshaun [Montgomery] on that second window dig — we’ve been working on that throughout the entire offseason.” That hard work paid off with real results. The team turned those extra yards into points and sustained drives. The chemistry is growing because the players put in the time to get better together. Coaching and Player Development Head coach Eli Drinkwitz praised the work of his position coach, Jacob Peeler. He said Peeler does a great job of pushing his players to be difference makers every single week. The players responded to that pressure on Saturday night. Drinkwitz said, “I think coach [Jacob] Peeler does an excellent job of challenging his guys each week to be difference makers, and they were tonight.” Donovan Olugbode led the team with 105 total yards, and 79 of those came after the catch. He showed great skill in open space, using a stiff arm to get into the end zone for a 60-yard score. Olugbode credited the practice drills for his success.

item.title: Tigers Add Gold Glove Infielder on One-Year Pact
item.description: Sep 26, 2026; Miami, Florida, USA; Atlanta Braves shortstop Ha-Seong Kim (7) gets the force out of Miami Marlins' Otto Lopez (6) at second base while attempting a double-play in the second inning at loanDepot Park. Mandatory Credit: Jim Rassol-Imagn Images The Detroit Tigers made their latest free-agent addition Tuesday, agreeing to terms with versatile infielder Ha-Seong Kim on a one-year, $5 million contract that includes up to $1 million in performance bonuses, according to multiple reports. The deal is pending a physical. Kim, 31, is a bounce-back bet after a difficult stretch. He posted strong numbers with the Padres earlier in his MLB career, including back-to-back seasons of 5-plus bWAR in 2022-23 and a Gold Glove in 2023. Injuries have limited him recently: a shoulder labrum tear in 2024, then a finger tendon injury that restricted him to 51 games and a .116/.219/.140 slash line with the Braves in 2026. When healthy, he has shown plus defense at shortstop, second base, and third base along with baserunning value. The signing fits a Tigers offseason that has prioritized pitching depth and roster flexibility after a 76-86 season. Earlier in November, Detroit signed reliever Emilio Pagán to a one-year, $11.5 million deal to replace the non-tendered Kenley Jansen as the closer. They also added former Yankees right-hander Luis Gil on a one-year, $2.3 million pact with incentives and locked up young starter Troy Melton on a six-year, $46.5 million extension. At the non-tender deadline, they kept most of their arbitration-eligible core (including Riley Greene, Spencer Torkelson, and Zach McKinstry) while non-tendering Matt Vierling, Trey Sweeney, and Jake Miller. President of baseball operations Scott Harris has indicated the club still wants additional relievers. With the CBA set to expire December 1, the remaining window for further additions is short. Kim gives Detroit a low-cost, multi-position defensive option while the front office continues to address the bullpen and evaluate starting pitching needs.
item.content:encoded: Sep 26, 2026; Miami, Florida, USA; Atlanta Braves shortstop Ha-Seong Kim (7) gets the force out of Miami Marlins' Otto Lopez (6) at second base while attempting a double-play in the second inning at loanDepot Park. Mandatory Credit: Jim Rassol-Imagn Images The Detroit Tigers made their latest free-agent addition Tuesday, agreeing to terms with versatile infielder Ha-Seong Kim on a one-year, $5 million contract that includes up to $1 million in performance bonuses, according to multiple reports. The deal is pending a physical. Kim, 31, is a bounce-back bet after a difficult stretch. He posted strong numbers with the Padres earlier in his MLB career, including back-to-back seasons of 5-plus bWAR in 2022-23 and a Gold Glove in 2023. Injuries have limited him recently: a shoulder labrum tear in 2024, then a finger tendon injury that restricted him to 51 games and a .116/.219/.140 slash line with the Braves in 2026. When healthy, he has shown plus defense at shortstop, second base, and third base along with baserunning value. The signing fits a Tigers offseason that has prioritized pitching depth and roster flexibility after a 76-86 season. Earlier in November, Detroit signed reliever Emilio Pagán to a one-year, $11.5 million deal to replace the non-tendered Kenley Jansen as the closer. They also added former Yankees right-hander Luis Gil on a one-year, $2.3 million pact with incentives and locked up young starter Troy Melton on a six-year, $46.5 million extension. At the non-tender deadline, they kept most of their arbitration-eligible core (including Riley Greene, Spencer Torkelson, and Zach McKinstry) while non-tendering Matt Vierling, Trey Sweeney, and Jake Miller. President of baseball operations Scott Harris has indicated the club still wants additional relievers. With the CBA set to expire December 1, the remaining window for further additions is short. Kim gives Detroit a low-cost, multi-position defensive option while the front office continues to address the bullpen and evaluate starting pitching needs.

item.title: Unaired Las Vegas radio reveals Red Bull considered giving up Max Verstappen's lead
item.description: Motorsport photo In almost any other Formula 1 race, suggesting a race leader deliberately surrender first place with one lap left would sound unthinkable. At the 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix, Red Bull’s pitwall genuinely floated the idea to Max Verstappen . Team radio messages revealed just how intensely Verstappen and race engineer Tom Hart calculated the closing stages of Saturday night’s 35-lead-change thriller. As early as Lap 39, Verstappen sensed Mercedes had deciphered his deployment pattern down the Strip and pressed his pitwall for a fresh plan. "You guys have to look at the plan for the final lap, because they have figured it out, that they can still [unclear] the line," Verstappen radioed. "So we need to see what we have to do for the final lap only." Hart replied that the strategy group had it "under discussion", before returning seven laps later on Lap 46 with a blunt verdict: "Deployment-wise, we don’t have anything better than the strategy you are doing at the moment. So final lap, you are already using the best strategy." Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing One lap later, Hart warned that the top five were stacked within a single second. Then came Lap 48, when George Russell locked up into the Turn 5 barrier while fighting team-mate Kimi Antonelli - drawing a sarcastic "Well done. My god," from Verstappen as his rival skidded off. That left 2026 world champion Antonelli as Verstappen’s sole remaining threat entering the penultimate tour. After warning of Turn 5 debris and updating the intervals, Hart delivered the boldest tactical prompt of the night midway through Lap 49. "Antonelli at 1.2, Piastri at 1.9. Just consider whether you want to be the lead car at the detection, Max. This is the penultimate lap," Hart told him. Hart’s logic centred on Las Vegas’s unique 2026 ruleset. With the circuit’s lone Overtake Mode detection point positioned immediately after the Turn 16 chicane, any driver trailing within one second there gained an extra 0.5 MJ of electrical deployment for the entire final lap - paired with a potent slipstream down the 1.9-kilometre Strip. Leading across that line risked turning Verstappen into a sitting duck before the chequered flag. Yet Verstappen never had to gamble on letting Antonelli through - because Mercedes’ teenager was trying to pull the exact same bluff in reverse. At the 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix, Red Bull’s pitwall genuinely floated the idea to Max Verstappen . As early as Lap 39, Verstappen sensed Mercedes had deciphered his deployment pattern down the Strip and pressed his pitwall for a fresh plan. "You guys have to look at the plan for the final lap, because they have figured it out, that they can still [unclear] the line," Verstappen radioed. "So we need to see what we have to do for the final lap only." Hart replied that the strategy group had it "under discussion", before returning seven laps later on Lap 46 with a blunt verdict: "Deployment-wise, we don’t have anything better than the strategy you are doing at the moment. So final lap, you are already using the best strategy." Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing One lap later, Hart warned that the top five were stacked within a single second. Then came Lap 48, when George Russell locked up into the Turn 5 barrier while fighting team-mate Kimi Antonelli - drawing a sarcastic "Well done. My god," from Verstappen as his rival skidded off. That left 2026 world champion Antonelli as Verstappen’s sole remaining threat entering the penultimate tour. After warning of Turn 5 debris and updating the intervals, Hart delivered the boldest tactical prompt of the night midway through Lap 49. "Antonelli at 1.2, Piastri at 1.9. Just consider whether you want to be the lead car at the detection, Max. This is the penultimate lap," Hart told him. Hart’s logic centred on Las Vegas’s unique 2026 ruleset. With the circuit’s lone Overtake Mode detection point positioned immediately after the Turn 16 chicane, any driver trailing within one second there gained an extra 0.5 MJ of electrical deployment for the entire final lap - paired with a potent slipstream down the 1.9-kilometre Strip. Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Aiming to stay behind Verstappen at the Turn 16 detection line and unleash a Mercedes final-lap battery push, Antonelli lifted off the throttle approaching Turn 14 on Lap 49 and gently reapplied power to maintain momentum. That unexpected pedal sequence disrupted his car’s energy-harvesting software, leaving him exiting the corner with zero battery and costing nearly two seconds down the straight. Both McLarens surged past before the final lap even began, transforming Hart’s Lap 50 briefing into a victory cruise. "Final lap, car behind, Norris," Hart informed Verstappen. "Norris 1.2, Piastri 2.4. And we can use boost exit Turn 14 regardless." Verstappen fired in a clean 1m36.450s final lap to beat Lando Norris by 0.639 seconds for his fourth win of 2026 - and 75th overall - stretching 37 points clear of Lewis Hamilton for second in the drivers’ championship while keeping Red Bull nine points ahead of McLaren for third in the constructors’ race entering Qatar. item.title: NFL Thanksgiving MEGA-preview: Packers vs. Rams must-win matchup, Lions & Bills defenses get tested
item.description: Subscribe to Football 301 with Nate Tice Apple Podcasts | Spotify | YouTube Nate Tice & Frank Schwab join forces to preview all five mid-week NFL Thanksgiving matchups. After airing out their thoughts on the Washington Commanders’ last-second win over the Cincinnati Bengals on Monday night, the duo dive into the Green Bay Packers battling the Los Angeles Rams on Wednesday night. With both teams’ playoff odds hanging in the balance, expect a kitchen sink matchup that should be a great appetizer for the rest of the Thanksgiving slate. Nate & Frank move on to the three Turkey Day matchups, including the Detroit Lions defense getting a true test in Caleb Williams & the Chicago Bears, the Dallas Cowboys and Philadelphia Eagles battling to stay relevant in the NFC East race and the Kansas City Chiefs giving the improving Buffalo Bills defense their toughest test of the season. The guys wrap things up with expectations for a Black Friday rock fight featuring the Denver Broncos & Pittsburgh Steelers. (3:15) - Commanders beat Rams on MNF (16:30) - Packers @ Rams (34:00) - Bears @ Lions (48:55) - Eagles @ Cowboys (1:00:30) - Chiefs @ Bills (1:20:05) - Broncos @ Steelers DETROIT, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 27: Jordan Love #10 of the Green Bay Packers takes a bite out of a turkey leg after the game against the Detroit Lions at Ford Field on November 27, 2025 in Detroit, Michigan. item.title: Bryce Young gets major vote of confidence from Panthers teammate Chuba Hubbard
item.description: Chuba Hubbard has backed Bryce Young with a strong message about the Carolina Panthers quarterback. The NFL running back has said that Young possesses abilities that coaches cannot teach. Speaking on the Pat McAfee Show, Hubbard discussed watching Young develop since joining Carolina. A.J. Hawk asked about the quarterback’s growth, consistency, and leadership throughout the week. “Yeah, I mean, Bryce has been a one-on-one player since he’s been with us,” Hubbard said. “Obviously won a Heisman for a reason.” MORE: NFL contenders & pretenders after Week 11 Hubbard then explained what separates Young from other quarterbacks. “I say the things he can do, you really can’t teach, you know,” he added. The running back pointed to Young’s ability to manipulate defenses and create opportunities for his teammates. “There’s certain plays where he can manipulate the defense, affect the linebackers, bring guys down to coverage, and then hit guys on the outside,” Hubbard said. He also praised Young’s leadership and their relationship away from the field. “And then obviously, he’s a great leader and a really good friend of mine. So I’m riding the Bryce Young train all year for sure,” Hubbard added. "The things he can do you really can't teach." Panthers' star Chuba Hubbard weighs in on Bryce Young on the @PatMcAfeeShow 💪 pic.twitter.com/LyLo011sm2 — NFL on ESPN (@ESPNNFL) November 24, 2026 Bryce Young and Carolina’s important stretch Charlotte, North Carolina, USA; Carolina Panthers head coach Dave Canales greets Carolina Panthers quarterback Bryce Young (9) at Bank of America Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jim Dedmon-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Young and Hubbard have helped Carolina remain competitive in the NFC South. The Panthers enter Week 12 with a 5-5 record after winning consecutive games. Their latest victory came against the Baltimore Ravens, with Young throwing for 254 yards and two touchdowns. Hubbard contributed 120 rushing yards and two rushing scores in the 35-33 win. Young has recorded 2,651 passing yards and 18 touchdowns through 10 games. He has also thrown seven interceptions, showing room for improvement despite Carolina’s recent progress. Meanwhile, Hubbard has added 831 rushing yards and nine touchdowns. His production gives Carolina a reliable ground option alongside Young’s passing ability. MORE: Panthers make wild franchise history in Week 10 win over Saints The Panthers still need greater consistency, particularly on defense. However, their offensive partnership provides a strong foundation. Hubbard’s comments also reflect the confidence Young has earned inside the locker room. Carolina will need that connection to continue as its playoff hopes develop. — Enjoy free coverage of the top news & trending stories with The Big Lead Newsletter —

item.title: Andy’s Player Ratings: Salford City 3-2 Sunderland u21 – Young Black Cats Bow Out
item.description: Isaac Allen : 8/10 Had no chance with the first and third goal, got something on the second but let the shot squirm underneath his body. Made some really good saves throughout though, including a really good double save in the first half and saving a one vs. one with his feet late on. Jenson Jones : 6/10 Looked good with the ball at his feet tonight, getting away from the press multiple times but had his hands full defensively. Ben Kindon : 6/10 Unlucky that his goal line clearance for the second immediately rebounded in off a Salford player at the back post. Otherwise he had a decent game despite the scoreline. Aji Alese : 6/10 Calm on the ball and strong in the tackle, not a stand out night but another game that he has come through unscathed. Joe Neild: 6/10 Let his man get in a cross far too easily for the opening goal but made up with it with a fantastic run and cross for the second goal. Liam Hunt: 6/10 Sat in front of the back four to provide them some protection and and rotated the ball from side to side well. Jaydon Jones : 8/10 Scored an astonishing goal from the halfway line to make it 1-1 and then made a great burst up the middle of the pitch to arrive late onto Neild’s cross into the box for the second equaliser. Was decent on the ball tonight, moving it about well. Abdoullah Ba: 5/10 Regularly showed his quick feet to turn away from a Salford player but we didn’t really see anything from him going forward and wasn’t quick enough to close down his man for the third goal by the hosts. Started in the #10 position but also drifted to the left and right wings. Jack Whittaker: 5/10 Buzzed around off the left wing but really struggled to get involved around the opposition box. Felix Scott : 5/10 Wasn’t in the game for long periods and then struggled to make an impact when the ball did come his way. Trey Ogunsuyi: 5/10 Tried to compete with the centre halves all night but found it difficult to keep hold of the ball and had no chances at all. Substitutes Charlie Dinsdale : 5/10 Replaced Ba but like the rest of our attacking players, just couldn’t get going. Bayley Hester : N/A A very late change after Jaydon Jones picked up a knock. Man of the Match: Jaydon Jones Isaac Allen ran him close but the man of the match has to be Jaydon Jones for his two goals. Created the first one himself after stealing the ball in the centre circle, looking up and firing past the goalkeeper from 45 yards. Then made a lung bursting late run into the six yard box to equalise yet again from a Joe Neild cross. His general play was tidy tonight and worked hard alongside Hunt in midfield.

item.title: Spire Returns $108K Check To JGR In Legal Spat
item.description: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images Spire Motorsports returned a check for $108,087.67 to Joe Gibbs Racing on Monday. This cash return shuts the door on any quick settlement for the team’s countersuit. The NASCAR world is watching as Spire rejects the money to force a judge to decide who is right. Per RacingNews.co , the team wants a court to officially rule in their favor rather than just pocketing the funds. Spire is asking the court to dismiss the need for a trial on the countersuit while still getting a legal win. The Money Was Never the Point JGR wrote the check to try and end the legal fight over a crew member trade. The team paid $100,000 plus interest to satisfy a claim Spire made about Robert “Cheddar” Smith. Spire claimed JGR owed them this amount because they failed to trade a similar employee back to Spire as agreed. JGR president Dave Alpern admitted under oath earlier this year that the deal was real. “So JGR agrees… JGR would pay Spire $100,000?” the question went during the deposition. Despite this admission, JGR tried to close the case with an unsolicited payment on November 6, 2026. They stated that the payment ended the controversy and that the counterclaims should be dismissed. Spire sees this as a cheap trick to avoid a real court judgment on the breach of contract. Spire says JGR has spent the last year trying to discredit them instead of fixing the problem. The team returned the check to prove they want a legal victory rather than just a payout. They are willing to wait for a trial date set for February 1, 2027, to get their answer. Why Spire Rejected the Cash Spire argues that JGR is in default on their counterclaims and cannot just pay their way out of a judgment. A filing on Monday night stated that JGR’s attempt to moot the issues is unsupported by law. Spire believes the payment was sent to avoid the defense JGR was already committed to fighting. “JGR would be happy to pay if we receive an invoice from Spire,” a JGR statement read before the check was returned. Spire says they did not want an invoice; they wanted the court to say JGR broke the rules. This stance puts the spotlight on the messy breakup between Chris Gabehart and his old team. The trial date remains set for Monday, February 1, 2027, regarding the lawsuit over Gabehart.

item.title: Celtics’ Joe Mazzulla Makes Feelings Clear Amid Four-Game Losing Streak
item.description: Boston Celtics head coach Joe Mazzulla during a game against the Atlanta Hawks in January 2026 Getty SAN FRANCISCO, CALIFORNIA - NOVEMBER 22: Jayson Tatum #0 of the Boston Celtics shoots a three-point shot over Draymond Green #23 of the Golden State Warriors in the first half of their game at Chase Center on November 22, 2026 in San Francisco, California. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) Getty Boston Celtics forwards Jayson Tatum and Paul George talk with head coach Joe Mazzulla. (Photo by Maddie Meyer/Getty Images) The Boston Celtics have not lost four straight games since the 2020-21 season. That changed Sunday in San Francisco, where an 88-87 loss to the Golden State Warriors gave Boston the first four-game slide of the Mazzulla era and its third consecutive blown fourth-quarter lead. The shooting numbers told the story again. Boston went 14-of-47 from beyond the arc and managed just 1-for-8 from deep in the fourth quarter. Jayson Tatum poured in 23 of his 27 points before halftime, then went 0-for-7 from the field after the break. The Celtics led 75-69 entering the final frame and watched it disappear. What Coach Mazzulla Said After the loss, Mazzulla was asked about the offensive struggles. “It’s inefficient, from the standpoint of shot making and execution,” Mazzulla said. “There’s an aspect that you have to trust through an 82-game season. To me their 20 offensive rebounds was a bigger issue than our offense or just as big of an issue.” Twenty offensive rebounds in a game you lose by one point. The Warriors turned those extra chances into 22 second-chance points. Mazzulla has watched the same pattern play out across all four losses, and the rebounding is the thread that connects them. “It’s both inefficient offense and our ability to finish possessions with the rebound,” Mazzulla said. “Those are the two trends that have stuck throughout the four games.” Getty SAN FRANCISCO, CALIFORNIA – NOVEMBER 22: Jayson Tatum #0 of the Boston Celtics shoots a three-point shot over Draymond Green #23 of the Golden State Warriors in the first half of their game at Chase Center on November 22, 2026 in San Francisco, California. (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) Mazzulla Draws a Line The Celtics were without Paul George (rest) and Mitchell Robinson (illness) on Sunday. Derrick White shot 6-of-21. The roster has been short-handed during the skid, but Mazzulla is not ready to panic with roughly three-quarters of the season still ahead. “If the season ended today, I’d be pretty concerned, but we have 64, 63 games left,” Mazzulla added. “If we’re getting good shots, you have to be able to trust over the course of the season that that’s going to work out. At some point you got to knock it down, whether it’s a layup or a fadeaway.” Then he made the dist

To me their 20 offensive rebounds was a bigger issue than our offense or just as big of an issue.” Twenty offensive rebounds in a game you lose by one point. The Warriors turned those extra chances into 22 second-chance points. Mazzulla has watched the same pattern play out across all four losses, and the rebounding is the thread that connects them. “It’s both inefficient offense and our ability to finish possessions with the rebound,” Mazzulla said. “Those are the two trends that have stuck throughout the four games.” Getty SAN FRANCISCO, CALIFORNIA – NOVEMBER 22: Jayson Tatum #0 of the Boston Celtics shoots a three-point shot over Draymond Green #23 of the Golden State Warriors in the first half of their game at Chase Center on November 22, 2026 in San Francisco, California. (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) Mazzulla Draws a Line The Celtics were without Paul George (rest) and Mitchell Robinson (illness) on Sunday. Derrick White shot 6-of-21. The roster has been short-handed during the skid, but Mazzulla is not ready to panic with roughly three-quarters of the season still ahead. “If the season ended today, I’d be pretty concerned, but we have 64, 63 games left,” Mazzulla added. “If we’re getting good shots, you have to be able to trust over the course of the season that that’s going to work out. At some point you got to knock it down, whether it’s a layup or a fadeaway.” Then he made the distinction that mattered most. “Our first shot defense has been very good. Our effort has been very good,” Mazzulla said. “When effort becomes an issue, that’s when I’ll be concerned.” Getty Boston Celtics forwards Jayson Tatum and Paul George talk with head coach Joe Mazzulla. (Photo by Maddie Meyer/Getty Images) Final Word for the Celtics A team with this much talent is not going to shoot 29 percent from three forever. Missed jumpers even out over 82 games. But giving up 20 offensive rebounds in a one-point loss is about effort and physicality, and it has shown up in all four games. Boston has Washington up next. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Celtics’ Joe Mazzulla Makes Feelings Clear Amid Four-Game Losing Streak appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: Newest Red Wings Netminder Used to Three-Goalie System
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect No one had to explain to new Detroit Red Wings netminder Samuel Montembeault the nuances of the three-goalie system. He was in the midst of one with the Montreal Canadiens . And now he’s entered into another goaler-a-trois with the Red Wings. Montembeault will be joining John Gibson and Daniil Tarasov in the battle for the Detroit goal crease. Sam Montembeault will wear #32 with Detroit. #LGRW pic.twitter.com/z8TMsS0jgY — NHL Rosters (@NHL_Rosters) November 24, 2026 In Montreal, Montembeault was dueling for the net with Jakub Dobes and Jacob Fowler . Toward the end of last season, he became the odd-man out. “Last year we had a three-goalie situation,” Montembeault said. “The whole playoff, I didn’t get a chance to play. And then the whole summer, there were some rumors.” Rumors turned into reality this week. Montembeault was part of the package leaving Montreal for Detroit in the blockbuster Dylan Larkin deal. New Red Wings Goalie Recovering From Injury Traditionally, three-goalie systems don’t work. There are only two nets on the ice for practice. One netminder is always on the outs, and none of the three is getting enough work. For the immediate future, that’s not going to be an issue. Montembeault is continuing his recovery from a lower-body injury and remains on IR. “Today was my first full practice with a team,” Montembeault said on Tuesday. “I was practicing in Montreal just with the goalie coach and a few extra players. So it’s all good to get out there and have a full, real practice.” SAM MONTEMBEAULT WHAT A SAVE!! 😱 pic.twitter.com/50HtF0r2gw — NHL (@NHL) March 18, 2025 That window of recovery gives Red Wings coach Todd McLellan time to sort out his netminding situation. “He’ll get evaluated physically and by our doctors as early as tomorrow,” McLellan said. “He needs more practice time with action going on around him and rebounds and all that type of stuff. “And then we’ll decide from there how we use the three of them and move on.” Red Wings Like What Montembeault Offers Montembeault wasn’t simply a throw-in to balance the salary cap books on the Larkin deal. “He’s wanted,” McLellan said. “We want him here. We think that he adds to the depth of the organization. “We’ll figure out how we’re going to use all these goaltenders.” Before his injury, Montembeault was assembling an impressive resume. He backstopped Canada to a world title. Canada selected him for the Four Nations Face-Off. Montembeault was under consideration for the 2026 Canadian Olympic team until being sidelined by injury. “It’s a tough position to come back from an injury, especially his,” McLellan said. “And they found two goaltenders that got hot. So unfortunately, things happen fast in this business, and it could change real quick. So you could never take a day for granted or anything like that. “And I’m not saying Sam did. item.title: Celtics Must Walk Away From Trey Murphy Trade Talk Now
item.description: Matthew Hinton-Imagn Images The Boston Celtics need to stop chasing a player they cannot get without giving up too much. The Pelicans are not moving Trey Murphy, and Boston should accept that hard truth right now. Fans want a boost, but the cost is simply too high for a team that already has a title ring. The Pelicans Hold All the Cards New Orleans is in no rush to trade its key wing player. Reports from Yahoo Sports indicate the team wants a massive haul in return. Jake Fischer wrote that the Pelicans remain reluctant to part with the in-demand swingman. This stance blocks any easy deal for the Celtics. Boston struggled in the past week, but panic buys often lead to regret. The front office must resist the urge to overpay just to fix a short slump. Even if the trade happens, the numbers do not look good for Boston. Murphy’s scoring average has dipped to 15.7 points this season. He shot 46.2 percent from the field and 37.7 percent from deep. Those are solid numbers, but they do not justify surrendering a future first-round pick and young talent. The Pelicans know their value, and they are willing to wait for the right offer. The Clippers Offer a Better Path While Boston chases a dead end, other teams are making bold moves. The Los Angeles Clippers are ready to sell before the Feb. 11 trade deadline. According to Marc Stein of The Stein Line, this represents one of the rare leaguewide squads viewed as a definite seller prior to the Feb. 11 trade deadline. They lost five first-round picks in a scandal and need to restock their assets. Boston could look at Darius Garland instead. He is playing well with career-high 21.3 points and 6.6 assists. One executive told Heavy.com that the Clippers have not quite started yet regarding the trade calls. However, when the new year arrives, Garland becomes the player for whom they can secure the highest return. The Celtics should keep their powder dry and wait for the right price on a player who actually wants to leave. The Warriors beat the Celtics on Sunday night, which shows the team still has work to do. But trading for a player who is not available is not the answer. The Pelicans are holding firm on their price. The Celtics must focus on the future, not a costly mistake in the present.

item.title: Minnesota QB Drake Lindsey Transfer Decision Poses Danger
item.description: STATE COLLEGE, PENNSYLVANIA - NOVEMBER 14: Drake Lindsey #5 of the Minnesota Golden Gophers throws the ball during the first quarter against the Penn State Nittany Lions at Beaver Stadium on November 14, 2026 in State College, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Isaiah Vazquez/Getty Images) Getty MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - NOVEMBER 07: Drake Lindsey #5 of the Minnesota Golden Gophers hands the ball off to Darius Taylor #1 against the UCLA Bruins in the first quarter at Huntington Bank Stadium on November 07, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by David Berding/Getty Images) MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - OCTOBER 24: Drake Lindsey #5 of the Minnesota Golden Gophers readies for play at the line of scrimmage against the Iowa Hawkeyes in the second quarter at Huntington Bank Stadium on October 24, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by David Berding/Getty Images) The Minnesota Golden Gophers have remained competitive in the Big Ten in recent seasons in part thanks to quarterback Drake Lindsey. It’s not clear with the offseason and transfer portal decisions approaching soon whether they’ll have one more year of that being true or not. Lindsey has another year of college football in him, assuming he doesn’t leave for the NFL, but it doesn’t seem guaranteed that he’ll spend it at Minnesota. He could choose instead to pursue a new opportunity — it’s a good offseason to be a QB transferring, because the expectation is that supply will be lighter than demand. Lindsey’s name was newly floated on Tuesday in an article by CBS Sports writer Brad Crawford , who sees a possible transfer in his future. Drake Lindsey Transfer Rumor Getty MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA – NOVEMBER 07: Drake Lindsey #5 of the Minnesota Golden Gophers hands the ball off to Darius Taylor #1 against the UCLA Bruins in the first quarter at Huntington Bank Stadium on November 07, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by David Berding/Getty Images) Crawford projects that Minnesota itself will have a new transfer quarterback as its starter in 2027 — because he believes Lindsey is a goner. “Drake Lindsey may have just played his last home game with the Golden Gophers over the weekend against Northwestern since there’s a chance the 6-5, 230-pound passer jumps and becomes a coveted option in the portal this cycle,” Crawford writes. “Lindsey hasn’t announced his plans, but hasn’t re-signed with Minnesota yet and may opt for a bigger spotlight elsewhere within the Power Four to try and enhance his future draft stock.” That push to a bigger program to grow his draft status would be a logical reason for Lindsey to at least consider a transfer. It’s not clear with the offseason and transfer portal decisions approaching soon whether they’ll have one more year of that being true or not. Lindsey’s name was newly floated on Tuesday in an article by CBS Sports writer Brad Crawford , who sees a possible transfer in his future. Drake Lindsey Transfer Rumor Getty MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA – NOVEMBER 07: Drake Lindsey #5 of the Minnesota Golden Gophers hands the ball off to Darius Taylor #1 against the UCLA Bruins in the first quarter at Huntington Bank Stadium on November 07, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by David Berding/Getty Images) Crawford projects that Minnesota itself will have a new transfer quarterback as its starter in 2027 — because he believes Lindsey is a goner. “Drake Lindsey may have just played his last home game with the Golden Gophers over the weekend against Northwestern since there’s a chance the 6-5, 230-pound passer jumps and becomes a coveted option in the portal this cycle,” Crawford writes. “Lindsey hasn’t announced his plans, but hasn’t re-signed with Minnesota yet and may opt for a bigger spotlight elsewhere within the Power Four to try and enhance his future draft stock.” That push to a bigger program to grow his draft status would be a logical reason for Lindsey to at least consider a transfer. There will obviously be financial implications, too. “Lindsey drew early-round buzz for 2027 before the season, but is not listed among the top-11 draft prospects at the position according to CBS Sports’ latest player rankings,” Crawford writes. “He was 14-10 as a starter approaching rivalry weekend and may be a good fit in a pro-style scheme elsewhere. Lindsey was one of Minnesota’s highest-paid players this season and one source said retention could be too costly. Minnesota also recently fired OC Greg Harbaugh Jr., who was instrumental in getting Lindsey to sign back in the day.” Minnesota finding a way to keep Lindsey would be a big statement for their program as a whole, but that could be easier said than done. College Football Reality Getty MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA – OCTOBER 24: Drake Lindsey #5 of the Minnesota Golden Gophers readies for play at the line of scrimmage against the Iowa Hawkeyes in the second quarter at Huntington Bank Stadium on October 24, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by David Berding/Getty Images) This really just sums up modern college football. Even when a program keeps a guy around for a few years, like Minnesota with Lindsey, the player often leaves eventually for a new opportunity. It wouldn’t reflect poorly on the Golden Gophers if Lindsey leaves. They did a great job to find him and develop him. Sometimes, with the market as free flowing as it is, players simply decide it’s time to look elsewhere. item.title: Krösche ‘operational’ with Milan announcement seemingly imminent
item.description: Krösche ‘operational’ with Milan announcement seemingly imminent Markus Krösche is already in Milan and hard at work, even though his appointment as the Rossoneri’s new Head of Football is yet to be made official. According to transfer expert Matteo Moretto, speaking on Fabrizio Romano’s YouTube channel, the German executive has already got down to business ahead of the January window. “Markus Krösche is already in Milan, already very operational, despite it not being official yet, but the announcement is expected shortly,” Moretto said, via MilanNews24 . Krösche has long been Gerry Cardinale’s first choice. DORTMUND, GERMANY – MAY 08: Markus Krosche, Sporting Director of Eintracht Frankfurt speaks to the media prior to the Bundesliga match between Borussia Dortmund and Eintracht Frankfurt at Signal Iduna Park on May 08, 2026 in Dortmund, Germany. (Photo by Leon Kügeler/Getty Images) On 18 October, he was released from his duties at Eintracht Frankfurt with immediate effect at his own request. Milan and Eintracht have now reportedly reached an agreement over compensation, exchanging documents yesterday, with the Rossoneri paying around €4m. Krösche’s first Milan tasks: Rabiot and Endrick Krösche’s first job will be Adrien Rabiot’s contract renewal. “There’s a lot of work going on over Rabiot’s renewal. Cardinale’s intention is to close it by the end of the year, because Rabiot is an indispensable player for Ruben Amorim,” Moretto explained. ITALY – NOVEMBER 8: Adrien Rabiot of Milan looks on during the Serie A match between Genoa CFC and AC Milan at Stadio Luigi Ferraris on November 8, 2026 in Genoa, Italy. (Photo by Simone Arveda/Getty Images) “Then we’ll see how the market develops. Milan want to strengthen up front, and Endrick is one name.” Rabiot is under contract until June 2028, and Milan are reportedly working towards a new deal until 2030. Cardinale said on Sunday that any January signing will only come if it’s “a move that counts”.

item.title: Ryan Day Identifies Biggest Challenge Ohio State Faces Against Michigan
item.description: Ohio State Buckeyes head coach Ryan Day is well aware of how well the Michigan defense has been playing this season despite the Wolverines’ struggling offense. Michigan is 6-5 this season and Ohio State is 7-4. The Wolverines are 17th in the country in scoring defense and 129th in scoring offense , according to ESPN. Ryan Day Says the Michigan Defense Leaves Little Margin for Error Day discussed what his team needs to worry about against the Wolverines, according to Eleven Warriors, which covered his Monday night appearance on the Buckeye Roundtable Show. “If we’re gonna focus on our record or anything like that, it’s just a distraction; it has to be all on winning this game,” Day said. He then turned to the Wolverines and what his own team has to clean up. “One of the better defenses in the entire country, so our margin for error’s tiny,” Day said. “We gotta be really tight with our plan and play clean. And then on defense, certainly we got to make improvements coming off of last week. We’ve got to do a good job fitting some of these quarterback runs; we know we’re gonna see some of those, and then, clearly, get off the field on third down.” Ohio State Buckeyes head coach Ryan Day and offensive lineman Luke Montgomery (51) celebrate in the first half of the NCAA football game against the Nebraska Cornhuskers at Memorial Stadium on Nov. 21, 2026 in Lincoln, Nebraska. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Michigan Wolverines Defense Held Ohio State Buckeyes to 10 Points in 2024 When the Buckeyes were 10-1 in 2024, they faced the Wolverines, who were 6-5 at the time. Michigan’s defense shut down Ohio State’s offense in that game. The Wolverines won by a final score of 13-10 . This time around, there are no playoff expectations for either team, but the stakes are high. The Ohio State and Michigan game means everything to the Wolverines’ players, coaches and fans, and the same goes for the Buckeyes’ side. It would be some story if Michigan’s defense stole another win in Columbus, Ohio, on Saturday, Nov. 28.

item.title: Athletics 2026 Season In Review: Kade Morris
item.description: Sep 4, 2026; Seattle, Washington, USA; Athletics starting pitcher Kade Morris (67) pitches to the Seattle Mariners during the first inning at T-Mobile Park. Mandatory Credit: Steven Bisig-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect This past season, the Athletics auditioned numerous pitchers in an unsuccessful effort to help their league-worst pitching staff keep opposing teams off the scoreboard. Right-hander Kade Morris, ranked among the team’s top-30 prospects, was among those given an opportunity, although the 24-year-old did not fare particularly well in his first taste of major league action. How was he acquired? Following a three-year collegiate career at the University of Nevada, the New York Mets selected Morris in the third round of the 2023 MLB Draft. At the 2024 trade deadline, the Mets dealt the young pitching prospect to the A’s in exchange for right-hander Paul Blackburn. Last season, Morris advanced to Triple-A Las Vegas in his first full season with his new organization, putting himself in position to make his MLB debut this season. What were the expectations? Expectations were relatively modest for Morris, who entered spring training as a non-roster invitee looking to make an impression on the major league coaching staff. Continued development and a strong showing at the highest level of the minor leagues helped pave the way for the Northern California native’s first big-league call-up. 2026 Results Morris spent the majority of the season with the A’s Triple-A affiliate, going 9-5 with a 4.08 ERA over 18 starts. Posting an ERA just above 4.00 in the hitter-friendly environment of Las Vegas Ballpark was enough to earn Morris his first opportunity against major league hitters. The right-hander bounced back and forth between Triple-A and the major leagues multiple times this year. Like several rookie pitchers, he struggled to retire opposing hitters, illustrating the significant gap between Triple-A and the majors. Morris went 0-1 with a 10.90 ERA and 2.13 WHIP in his first six major league appearances, including his first two starts. 2027 Outlook Morris, who projects as a back-of-the-rotation starter or swingman, will compete in spring training for a spot in the A’s rotation or a long-relief role. If he fails to earn an Opening Day roster spot, he will likely begin the season in Triple-A, where he can continue developing while waiting for an opportunity to join the Athletics’ pitching staff. At the moment, the final two spots in the A’s rotation remain unsettled, with J.T. Ginn, Luis Severino and Gage Jump presumably in line to fill three spots in the starting five, health permitting. The Athletics bullpen is even more unpredictable after left-hander Hogan Harris and right-hander Luis Medina were the only two relievers to consistently perform well this past season. Will Morris take the next step and secure a role with the A’s next season, or will he become another disappointing trade acquisition? What are your expectations for

item.title: Legendary HOF Voter Supports Induction of Hines Ward Into Canton
item.description: 21 November 2010: Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver Hines Ward (86) runs to the 16 yardline after catching a Ben Roethlisberger pass during the first quarter of the Pittsburgh Steelers 35-3 victory against the Oakland Raiders at Heinz Field in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. On Nov. 24, the Pro Football Hall of Fame announced that 52 players, including 30 offensive and 22 defensive players have advanced to the next round of voting for the Class of 2027, which includes former Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Ben Roethlisberger, as well as five other former Steelers players. One of those former players is wide receiver Hines Ward , who former Pro Football Hall of Fame voter Peter King believes it is time for Canton to immortalize his trademark grin in bronze. View this post on Instagram “Oh, I think so. He’s the best blocking wide receiver in this century, and he caught 1,000 balls,” King said when discussing whether Ward deserves to hear his name called when the Class of 2027 is announced at NFL Honors in Los Angeles during Super Bowl week in February. “He overachieved massively. He had a big Super Bowl, he was a huge contributor to a big Super Bowl win for the Steelers, and always played well in big games. He was a ridiculous, feisty competitor. I supported his case for the Hall of Fame.” Ward has been a Pro Football Hall of Fame semifinalist for 10 straight years from 2017-26 . After playing for the Georgia Bulldogs, Ward was selected in the third round of the 1998 NFL Draft by the Steelers, and he played his entire professional career in Pittsburgh. Hines Ward has been a Pro Football Hall of Fame semifinalist for 10 straight years from 2017-26 . After playing for the Georgia Bulldogs, Ward was selected in the third round of the 1998 NFL Draft by the Steelers, and he played his entire professional career in Pittsburgh. Over his 14-year career, Ward had 1,000 career receptions (No.18 all-time) for 12,083 yards and 85 touchdowns. Along with his amazing catching ability and sure hands, Ward was also known for his excellent blocking ability. Ward was the MVP of Super Bowl XL after leading the Steelers to a 21-10 victory over the Seattle Seahawks, and in three Super Bowls, Ward has 14 receptions for 244 yards and two touchdowns. In 2008, Ward was the Steelers’ Walter Payton NFL Man of the Year nominee, and he was selected to the Pro Bowl four times from 2002-05, and was a member of the Steelers’ 75th Season All-Time Team. Ward was selected by his teammates as the Steelers MVP three times in his career, including in 2002 with Joey Porter , 2003, and 2005 with Casey Hampton . NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Matthew Stockman/Getty Images) Getty Minnesota Timberwolves guard Donte DiVincenzo is targeting his 2026-2027 season debut around Jan. 1, shortly before or after the New Year, as he recovers from a torn right Achilles tendon. According to ESPN’s Shams Charania, the Timberwolves officially cleared DiVincenzo to return to team basketball activities, marking a major milestone just seven months after he underwent surgery on April 26. Minnesota Timberwolves guard Donte DiVincenzo is targeting his season debut shortly before or after the New Year, sources tell ESPN, receiving full clearance for team activities and successfully completing five-on-five scrimmages in recent weeks. It would mark a return in just… pic.twitter.com/XJIjO99bpf — Shams Charania (@ShamsCharania) November 24, 2026 How Donte DiVincenzo Get the Injury? Getty DALLAS, TEXAS – MARCH 30: Donte DiVincenzo #0 and Ayo Dosunmu #13 of the Minnesota Timberwolves celebrate after a score during the first quarter against the Dallas Mavericks at American Airlines Center on March 30, 2026 in Dallas, Texas. (Photo by Sam Hodde/Getty Images) He suffered the injury in the opening minutes of Game 4 during Minnesota’s first-round playoff series against the Denver Nuggets in April. After spending the summer rehabilitating at the team facility, DiVincenzo will now begin practicing with the squad so trainers can monitor how his body responds before locking in an exact return date. With the announcement, he is progressing ahead of the typical nine-to-twelve-month timeline Nonetheless, DiVincenzo remains ruled out for immediate game action as he transitions back into team practices and full-contact work. Donte DiVincenzo Speaks About His Mindset This Season Despite Injury Getty DENVER, COLORADO – APRIL 20: Donte DiVincenzo #0 of the Minnesota Timberwolves is congratulated by Aex Rodriguez after their win against the Denver Nuggets during Game Two of the First Round of the NBA Western Conference Playoffs at Ball Arena on April 20, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Matthew Stockman/Getty Images) Donte DiVincenzo has approached his recovery from a ruptured right Achilles tendon with an aggressive and work-first mindset. DiVincenzo stayed in Minnesota over the summer for rehab and said he “fell in love with the process” of putting in the work day after day. He has noted in an interview with The Athletic that his instinct is to push constantly, with medical staff sometimes having to hold him back rather than urge him forward. “I wouldn’t come in here with the mindset of I’m gonna play next year,” he said before the training camp. “No, the mindset is to play this year.” “It’s been very, very helpful those days or weeks where you feel like you’re not gaining so much ground as you should. You talk to those guys, and they kind of help push you along.” He described the start of training camp as a “gut punch” when teammates returned to the court and he could not play yet. DiVincenzo credited the Timberwolves’ front office, coaches, and players for keeping him involved in everything so he still felt part of the group. According to DiVincenzo, watching games and halftime from the locker room has helped him study spacing, slot cuts, and how to make the game easier for teammates when he returns. He opened up about the mental battles of being injured this season. “There [are] a lot of battles in sports that aren’t the physical ones,” he said. “It starts with the physical and then turns into the mental side. So, just [showing] that there is light at the end of the tunnel. As vulnerable as I am, I can tell you I’m as driven and as confident.” “Sometimes, you just want to get something off of your chest and leave it alone and go forward from there. It doesn’t need to have a resolution every single day. So, just being that for them and whatever they need as the season evolves.” Last season, he recorded 12.2 points, 4.1 rebounds, 3.8 assists, and 1.3 steals per game while committing 1.4 turnovers. He shot 40.6% from the field overall and 37.9% from three-point range on 7.9 attempts per game. DiVincenzo will help the Timberwolves this season by adding 3-point shooting, backcourt depth, and locker-room leadership for a new-look roster led by LaMelo Ball. item.title: Jordan Spieth Dealt Concerning News Ahead of 2027 PGA Tour Season
item.description: Jordan Spieth looks on. Getty Jordan Spieth recently hosted a successful junior championship with Under Armour. The inaugural event ran Oct. 16-18 in Dallas. He took time out of his day to chat with every child who competed. The weekend was a success. His year and recent career tell a different story. Spieth owns three major titles. He is just the Wanamaker Trophy away from completing the career Grand Slam. Yet he now struggles to crack the top 10 in PGA Tour fields. He made 22 PGA Tour starts in 2026. None finished in the top 10. His last win, one of 13 on the PGA Tour, came at the 2022 RBC Heritage. So what went wrong? Jordan Spieth Dealt Concerning News Spieth’s swing motion is very different from what it was before. Prehension Athletics compared a 2018 frame of Spieth’s swing with a recent one. Back at his peak, his lead shoulder finished higher. Now his club finishes higher. Jordan Spieth was the #2 ranked golfer in the world in 2018… He’s currently ranked #70…. Look how different his arms move in his swing when he’s good vs when he struggles (2018 on the right)…. There are 5 unique muscles on each side of the forearm that work in pairs to move… pic.twitter.com/AhSoz8O7Hm — Prehension Athletics (@tommym8) November 19, 2026 Spieth no longer swings with the same muscles. The forearm muscles work in pairs to move the arms in the golf swing. “Jordan uses his palmaris longus and extensor carpi radialis brevis when he’s at his best,” they said. “He uses flexor carpi ulnaris or radialis and extensor carpi radialis or ulnaris when he’s at his worst,” they added. Forearm flexors create gripping force, while extensors stabilize the wrist. A different muscle mix can change how the wrist holds the clubface through impact. The “worst” list includes the extensor carpi ulnaris. A British Journal of Sports Medicine study of European Tour golfers found 67% of wrist injuries hit the leading wrist. The most significant injury, measured by missed competition, involved the extensor carpi ulnaris tendon. Spieth knows that tendon well. He had surgery on Aug. 21, 2024, to rebuild the sheath around it in his left wrist. That overlap does not prove cause. Jordan Spieth Tells Confident, But Data Tells A Different Story Spieth feels confident in his swing. After the St. Jude Championship, he said he felt he was “getting back to playing really good golf.” In Japan, he said, “I feel that my mechanics are more sound than they’ve been for a while.” The results have not followed. Rex Hoggard, a senior writer for Golf Channel, discussed the relegation risk on the Golf Channel Podcast. He said Tour CEO Brian Rolapp wants young talent to arrive sooner. The new system will “shorten PGA Tour careers, simply as a matter of math,” Hoggard said. He called at least one slump “almost inevitable.” Hoggard used Spieth as his example. “This system is going to shorten PGA Tour careers, simply as a matter of math,” he said . It is high time he changed some things to bring his career back. After the regular season, the fall brought no rescue. Spieth did not make the final Aon Next 10. That leaves him without a guaranteed spot at the AT&T Pebble Beach Pro-Am and the Genesis Invitational. item.description: ⚽ Live coverage from six 8pm GMT kick-offs ⚽ De Bruyne’s return reminds City what they are missing ⚽ Live scores | League phase standings | Email Simon There’s been a shot on target now, and it’s only gone in! It’s from a corner – one of those where the defender ushers the ball out of play thinking he’s about to get a goal-kick only for the fourth official to point to the corner – from which Yilmaz heads goalwards, the ball loops up off Jackson, and Deniz Gul heads it in! Not only that, just after he does so he gets volleyed in the face by Nicolas Jackson, who was a bit late in trying to clear the ball. The two early kick-offs are now into their 75th minute, and still none of the four teams have had a shot on target. Galatasaray and Aston Villa are currently drawing 2-2 on shots off target and 0-0 on actual goals, while Bodo/Glimt and Lask are drawing 3-3 on shots off target and 0-0 on actual goals. Continue reading...

item.title: Seahawks sign offensive tackle off Bills’ practice squad
item.description: (Photo by Timothy T Ludwig/Getty Images) | Getty Images A day after veteran tackle Bobby Hart was signed to the 53-man roster , the Seattle Seahawks have added another offensive lineman to the roster. The team signed tackle Chase Lundt off the Buffalo Bills’ practice squad, The Ringer ’s Tom Pelissero reported on Tuesday. In a corresponding move, cornerback Avery Smith was waived by the Seahawks. The Seahawks are signing OT Chase Lundt off the Bills practice squad, per source. To make room, Seattle is waiving CB Avery Smith. — Tom Pelissero (@TomPelissero) November 24, 2026 The 26-year-old Lundt was a sixth-round pick of the Bills in the 2025 NFL Draft, and played two games in a rookie season spent on their active roster. After he was waived during roster cuts ahead of the 2026 season, he was signed to their practice squad where he had remained until Tuesday. A four-year starter at UConn, Lundt was a collegiate teammate of former Seattle guard Christian Haynes, now of the Miami Dolphins. Lundt and Hart both joining the roster appear to be insurance for right tackle Abe Lucas, who is dealing with an ankle injury and is a question mark for Week 12 against the San Francisco 49ers. Smith’s departure from the Seahawks comes a day after veteran Trevon Diggs, like Hart, was signed to the active roster off the practice squad. The 22-year-old appeared in six games with Seattle after the team acquired him from the L.A. Chargers for a sixth-round pick ahead of the regular season . After moving a 2027 day-three selection in order to acquire Smith just a few months ago, the Seahawks will presumably be interested in signing him to their practice squad, should he clear waivers.

item.title: Yankees trade idea parts with three top prospects to land A's All-Star catcher
item.description: Yankees trade idea parts with three top prospects to land A's All-Star catcher originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . This offseason, the New York Yankees are likely looking to make a few additions to the lineup, with their eyes potentially set on outfield, second base, and maybe even third base upgrades. But that's not all this team could be on the hunt for. Adding a new starting catcher would make sense, as they tried to make such a move at the 2026 MLB trade deadline, but came up short. The free agent catcher pool is weak, but the trade market has some fun options. Hunter Goodman of the Colorado Rockies would be great, but ESPN's Tristan Cockcroft shared a different trade idea, one that would have the Yankees sending three top prospects to the Athletics in exchange for All-Star catcher Shea Langeliers. Yankees trade idea lands Shea Langeliers for 3 prospects "Trade Carlos Lagrange, Elmer Rodriguez and Cade Smith (no, not that one) to the Athletics for Shea Langeliers," Cockcroft writes. With Langeliers under club control for the 2027 and 2028 seasons, the Yankees would be getting two years out of a young, elite power-hitting catcher with plenty of upside. Last season, despite missing a good chunk of the year, Langeliers hit 23 homers with 111 hits, a .262 batting average, and an .802 OPS to go with his first All-Star nod. The year prior, he had an .861 OPS with a .277 batting average and 31 homers. He's posted 3.5 and 3.3 bWAR the past two seasons, and has become one of the best catchers in baseball. MORE : Brian Cashman's latest comments opens door to Jasson Dominguez trade for Yankees Acquiring such a player won't come cheap, and that's why the proposed trade idea from Cockcroft would have the Yankees giving up so much value for just two seasons out of Langeliers. Lagrange and Rodriguez are two premier pitching prospects in the Yankees' farm system, and Smith is a good pitching prospect as well. The A's are in dire need of good young pitching, and trading Langeliers for three high-upside starters from the Yankees in this idea would make a lot of sense, especially since extending Langeliers will prove tricky. For the Yankees, spending so much on Langeliers is a bit risky, but the upside of getting such a talented catcher is well worth it. He'd be a huge upgrade for New York's offense and give this lineup an elite power-hitting option at the catcher spot. item.title: New York Jets Suddenly Release 2 Players After Chargers Win
item.description: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - NOVEMBER 15: Head coach Aaron Glenn of the New York Jets looks on before a game against the Buffalo Bills at MetLife Stadium on November 15, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Sarah Stier/Getty Images) Getty The New York Jets finally got back in the win column on Sunday, defeating the Los Angeles Chargers 27-24 to snap a five-game losing streak and improve to 3-8 on the season. Now, heading into the holiday week, the Jets will turn their attention to another winnable matchup against the 1-9 Miami Dolphins. However, Miami’s only win this season came against New York earlier in the year. Jets Suddenly Release 2 Players After Chargers Win Following Sunday’s victory, the Jets reportedly made a couple of roster moves along the defensive line. According to Brian Costello of the New York Post, New York is waiving defensive tackle Payton Page, who could return to the practice squad if he clears waivers. The team is also releasing defensive tackle Isaiahh Loudermilk from its practice squad. “The Jets are waiving DT Payton Page, per source,” Costello reported on X. “He could return to the practice squad if he clears waivers. They are also releasing DT Isaiahh Loudermilk from the p squad.” The Jets are waiving DT Payton Page, per source. He could return to the practice squad if he clears waivers. They are also releasing DT Isaiahh Loudermilk from the p squad. — Brian Costello (@BrianCoz) November 24, 2026 These moves likely clear the way for David Onyemata to return to the 53-man roster this week after the Jets designated him to return from injured reserve and opened his 21-day practice window. New York also welcomed starting nose tackle Harrison Phillips back to the lineup in Week 11 against the Chargers. With the defensive line getting healthier, the Jets had to make a few corresponding roster moves. Looking at the Jets New York finds itself in an unusual position, and how the rest of this season unfolds could play a major role in determining the team’s direction moving forward. The Jets currently hold two potential top-five picks in next year’s draft. They have their own first-round pick and also own the rights to the Indianapolis Colts’ selection. With both picks currently in the top five, keeping them in that range could become a priority. At the same time, head coach Aaron Glenn could use a late-season winning streak to strengthen his case to remain in New York. His job security remains uncertain as he’s in the back half of his second season with the organization. Glenn went 3-14 in his first year, and unless the Jets put together a remarkable run to close out this season, he could face an uphill battle to keep his job. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post New York Jets Suddenly Release 2 Players After Chargers Win appeared first on HEAVY .
