item.title: Kyle DeVan’s Intensity Drives Bears Offensive Line Success
item.description: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images The Chicago Bears offensive line found its voice not with a cheer, but with a scowl. After a win against the New England Patriots, assistant coach Kyle DeVan looked like someone had shot his dog, according to reports. This was not a moment of celebration for the 41-year-old coach, even though the team won from start to finish on a short week. DeVan explained his reaction with brutal honesty, stating, “I want to win every game and I want us to play the best we can, and when we don’t, I get a little not happy,” per the Chicago Tribune . That specific intensity is now the fuel the Bears are betting on to fix their line issues. Johnson’s Deliberate Plan Head coach Ben Johnson did not stumble into this pairing by accident. The Bears constructed Johnson’s first staff in February 2025 with a clear goal: find a younger assistant to work in tandem with veteran Dan Roushar. Johnson wants to develop young draft picks like Luke Newman into future starters once veterans move on. He openly admits that he drops DeVan’s name regularly on purpose to get him noticed by other teams. “I’m glad you caught that,” Johnson said of his references to DeVan, noting that the spotlight is by intent, per the Chicago Tribune. This strategy helps DeVan grow while keeping the Bears’ development pipeline strong. Strength in the Trenches The physical preparation for this line goes beyond just blocking schemes. Assistant strength and conditioning coach Mark Philippi brings a unique background that has the internet buzzing. A former world champion powerlifter, Philippi has qualified for the World’s Strongest Man competition seven times. Christian D’Andrea of For The Win joked that Philippi is the “final boss all other strength coaches must strive to defeat,” according to Sports Illustrated . Some fans even suggested the team should “suit up Mark Philippi” to solve their offensive line problems. Philippi’s presence ensures the players have the raw power to match DeVan’s technical demands. A Lesson in Celebration DeVan eventually learned that a win is hard to do and deserves a moment of joy. After being fined $100 by his linemen for his lack of celebration, he adjusted his approach. “I learned my lesson,” DeVan said. “I celebrate everything. I’ve been in this thing. A win is hard to do,” per the Chicago Tribune. This shift shows a coach who cares deeply about the process but respects the final result. The Bears face a tough test on Thursday, Nov. 26, at Ford Field against the Detroit Lions.

item.title: How Micah Ford flipped ignominious era for Stanford football into his personal legacy
item.description: Micah Ford #20 of the Stanford Cardinal looks on before a game against the Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets on Sept. 26, 2026 at Stanford Stadium in Palo Alto, Calif. (Matthew Huang/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) Micah Ford has witnessed the lows of this Stanford football era. In November 2024, as a freshman, he watched from the California Memorial Stadium sideline as quarterback Fernando Mendoza went "98 yards with my boys" to lead an epic Big Game comeback, handing Stanford its first four-game losing streak against Cal since 2005. He was in the building four months later, when recently hired general manager Andrew Luck fired Troy Taylor, the head coach who had recruited him, citing the need for a "reset" after an investigation concluded that Taylor had bullied and belittled female staffers. Ford saw all of it. The 3-9 season in 2024. The 4-8 campaign a year ago. The slow start this season. He played for one head coach as a freshman (Taylor), then another as a sophomore (interim Frank Reich), and now another as a junior playing for first-year head coach Tavita Pritchard. Chaos and turmoil were all he knew. Midway through October, the feeling couldn't have been much better. The Cardinal were 2-4, and each blowout loss looked worse than the last. His team lost those games by a combined 172 points. Ford, the engine of the offense at running back, wasn't producing. But after that 58-7 loss to then-No. 6 Notre Dame on Oct. 10, something changed. Stanford, led by Ford's sudden emergence, became an unrecognizable football team. The first six games of Ford's season: 95 carries, 350 yards (3.7 yards per carry) and four rushing touchdowns. The last five: 108 carries, 701 yards (6.5 YPC) and nine rushing touchdowns. His yardage totals, including receptions, in each of those games were 231, 208, 120, 150 and 156. He's been the most consistent presence for an offense that desperately needed it under fourth-year running backs coach Malcolm Agnew. Ford's success directly led to Stanford's (6-5, 4-4 ACC) success. The Cardinal have won four of their last five games. They destroyed Cal 44-28 in Saturday's Big Game and earned bowl-game eligibility for the first time since 2018. Looking back, Ford can easily say it was all worth it. "To be at a program where, obviously, I didn't have success early, and then to see it gel into the program that we knew it could be," Ford said Saturday, "it's kind of just, like, I'm at a loss of words for it. "Honestly, there was no way we were leaving without that axe today," he added, after rushing for 151 yards and two touchdowns. "I don't know how long (it's been since) Stanford kept it two years in a row. It's probably been a little while." Ford is correct. The last time Stanford won consecutive games against Cal was in 2018, the last of a dominant nine-year Big Game run. Following that season, the Bears won five of six matchups from 2019-2024. Stanford has since won two in a row, in many ways thanks to Ford, a Big Game killer. A y
item.content:encoded: Micah Ford #20 of the Stanford Cardinal looks on before a game against the Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets on Sept. 26, 2026 at Stanford Stadium in Palo Alto, Calif. (Matthew Huang/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) Micah Ford has witnessed the lows of this Stanford football era. In November 2024, as a freshman, he watched from the California Memorial Stadium sideline as quarterback Fernando Mendoza went "98 yards with my boys" to lead an epic Big Game comeback, handing Stanford its first four-game losing streak against Cal since 2005. He was in the building four months later, when recently hired general manager Andrew Luck fired Troy Taylor, the head coach who had recruited him, citing the need for a "reset" after an investigation concluded that Taylor had bullied and belittled female staffers. Ford saw all of it. The 3-9 season in 2024. The 4-8 campaign a year ago. The slow start this season. He played for one head coach as a freshman (Taylor), then another as a sophomore (interim Frank Reich), and now another as a junior playing for first-year head coach Tavita Pritchard. Chaos and turmoil were all he knew. Midway through October, the feeling couldn't have been much better. The Cardinal were 2-4, and each blowout loss looked worse than the last. His team lost those games by a combined 172 points. Ford, the engine of the offense at running back, wasn't producing. But after that 58-7 loss to then-No. 6 Notre Dame on Oct. 10, something changed. Stanford, led by Ford's sudden emergence, became an unrecognizable football team. The first six games of Ford's season: 95 carries, 350 yards (3.7 yards per carry) and four rushing touchdowns. The last five: 108 carries, 701 yards (6.5 YPC) and nine rushing touchdowns. His yardage totals, including receptions, in each of those games were 231, 208, 120, 150 and 156. He's been the most consistent presence for an offense that desperately needed it under fourth-year running backs coach Malcolm Agnew. Ford's success directly led to Stanford's (6-5, 4-4 ACC) success. The Cardinal have won four of their last five games. They destroyed Cal 44-28 in Saturday's Big Game and earned bowl-game eligibility for the first time since 2018. Looking back, Ford can easily say it was all worth it. "To be at a program where, obviously, I didn't have success early, and then to see it gel into the program that we knew it could be," Ford said Saturday, "it's kind of just, like, I'm at a loss of words for it. "Honestly, there was no way we were leaving without that axe today," he added, after rushing for 151 yards and two touchdowns. "I don't know how long (it's been since) Stanford kept it two years in a row. It's probably been a little while." Ford is correct. The last time Stanford won consecutive games against Cal was in 2018, the last of a dominant nine-year Big Game run. Following that season, the Bears won five of six matchups from 2019-2024. Stanford has since won two in a row, in many ways thanks to Ford, a Big Game killer. A year ago, when the Cardinal blew out Cal 31-10 in Palo Alto, he rushed 29 times for 150 yards and a touchdown. Ford did everything for the Cardinal again on Saturday. He recorded six rushes of 10 or more yards, including a 63-yard touchdown that put Stanford up by 16 and essentially sealed the result in the third quarter. He threw a one-yard touchdown pass on a trick play to tight end Chico Holt for the game's first score. That brought back memories for Ford, who was a high school quarterback at Toms River North (N.J.). "It's kind of like riding a bike," he said. "You never really lose that." On Saturday, Ford became Stanford's first thousand-yard rusher since 2017 (Bryce Love), reaching 1,051 yards with one more regular-season game remaining. He has been one of the most consistent and productive running backs in college football, ranking 13th in carries, 17th in rushing yards and 11th in rushing touchdowns. Ford is tied for the FBS lead with four games scoring at least three total touchdowns. Ford was Stanford's most experienced offensive skill-position player entering the season. Only three other returners recorded more than 100 yards in 2025, and Ford led the group. Pritchard, in his first season at the helm, has relied heavily on his bell-cow running back - especially as the long season has worn on. And Ford has delivered. What changed after that slow start? "The competitive cauldron that we've created on our practice field is the reason for what you're asking about," Pritchard said. "The reason our run game has gotten better, the reason that all our units have gotten progressively better throughout the year, is the work that our guys put in on the practice field and in the building. And so, the run game is no different. The way that those guys have applied themselves and have bought into what we're doing. They learn, and they trust the coaches to get them coached up, and there's a lot of honesty when it comes to getting better." Ford also pointed to the offensive line as a major reason for his breakout. "I go as far as they go," he said Saturday. "Without them, it's definitely not possible." The Big Game win was doubly rewarding. By avenging that painful 2024 loss at Memorial Stadium, Ford and his teammates also potentially earned one more game together. Which bowl game the Cardinal might play in will be determined by the result of their final regular-season contest Saturday against SMU. "To get those seniors an extra game and have them be a part of something, be a part of this turnaround," Ford said, "it's just great." Subscribe There’s more to San Francisco with the Chronicle. Subscribe today for just 25¢. This article originally published at How Micah Ford flipped ignominious era for Stanford football into his personal legacy .

item.title: MLB Pitch-Rigging Case Turns to Shocking Personal Texts
item.description: Jul 26, 2025; Kansas City, Missouri, USA; Cleveland Guardians relief pitcher Emmanuel Clase (48) delivers a pitch against the Kansas City Royals in the ninth inning at Kauffman Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Denny Medley-Imagn Images The federal trial of former Cleveland Guardians pitchers Emmanuel Clase and Luis Ortiz continues this week in Brooklyn, with testimony focusing on the two June 2025 pitches prosecutors say Ortiz deliberately threw outside the strike zone in exchange for payments. Jurors have heard from a FanDuel executive that six wagers on Ortiz’s first pitch of the third inning on June 27 against the Cardinals generated more than $19,000 in winnings and led the sportsbook to suspend four accounts the next day. Those same accounts had also placed bets on an Ortiz pitch from June 15. Prosecutors argue those flagged bets helped launch the broader investigation. A cooperating witness, Enthony Diaz, has testified that he netted more than $31,000 on wagers tied to the two pitches Ortiz is accused of rigging. On the same June 27 date, prosecutors introduced WhatsApp messages between Ortiz and his wife that included the lines “Delete the evidence,” “What if he’s undercover?” and “Luis, it’s your future.” Ortiz has pleaded not guilty. His defense maintains he never communicated with the bettors and that the government’s case against him is thin. Clase, the former All-Star closer, is accused of providing information on roughly 18 pitches across three seasons (beginning in 2023) and recruiting Ortiz into the scheme in 2025. Both players face charges of conspiracy to commit wire fraud, honest-services wire fraud, sports bribery, and money laundering. They remain on unpaid leave from the Guardians and are considered highly unlikely to pitch in the majors again regardless of the trial outcome. Prosecutors have indicated they expect to rest their case around Thanksgiving, with closing arguments and a possible verdict in early December. MLB continues its own investigation parallel to the criminal proceedings.
item.content:encoded: Jul 26, 2025; Kansas City, Missouri, USA; Cleveland Guardians relief pitcher Emmanuel Clase (48) delivers a pitch against the Kansas City Royals in the ninth inning at Kauffman Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Denny Medley-Imagn Images The federal trial of former Cleveland Guardians pitchers Emmanuel Clase and Luis Ortiz continues this week in Brooklyn, with testimony focusing on the two June 2025 pitches prosecutors say Ortiz deliberately threw outside the strike zone in exchange for payments. Jurors have heard from a FanDuel executive that six wagers on Ortiz’s first pitch of the third inning on June 27 against the Cardinals generated more than $19,000 in winnings and led the sportsbook to suspend four accounts the next day. Those same accounts had also placed bets on an Ortiz pitch from June 15. Prosecutors argue those flagged bets helped launch the broader investigation. A cooperating witness, Enthony Diaz, has testified that he netted more than $31,000 on wagers tied to the two pitches Ortiz is accused of rigging. On the same June 27 date, prosecutors introduced WhatsApp messages between Ortiz and his wife that included the lines “Delete the evidence,” “What if he’s undercover?” and “Luis, it’s your future.” Ortiz has pleaded not guilty. His defense maintains he never communicated with the bettors and that the government’s case against him is thin. Clase, the former All-Star closer, is accused of providing information on roughly 18 pitches across three seasons (beginning in 2023) and recruiting Ortiz into the scheme in 2025. Both players face charges of conspiracy to commit wire fraud, honest-services wire fraud, sports bribery, and money laundering. They remain on unpaid leave from the Guardians and are considered highly unlikely to pitch in the majors again regardless of the trial outcome. Prosecutors have indicated they expect to rest their case around Thanksgiving, with closing arguments and a possible verdict in early December. MLB continues its own investigation parallel to the criminal proceedings.

item.title: Brazil U17's Kauê Furquim named man of the match v Tanzania, thanks team
item.description: Brazil U17's Kauê Furquim named man of the match v Tanzania, thanks team Number 7 named player of the match in win over Tanzania Credits: Handout /CBF Named player of the match in Brazil’s 1-0 win over Tanzania on Tuesday (24) at the U-17 World Cup, Kauê Furquim celebrated the individual recognition and shared the credit with his national team teammates, the coaching staff and his family. The forward also spoke about the importance of staying focused as the competition progresses. “First of all, I want to thank God, the national team and everyone in our squad. Without them, I wouldn’t have achieved this. I also want to thank my family and all my staff. I’m very happy to have won this award,” said the Bahia forward. Kauê also celebrated the result and Brazil’s qualification for the second round of the World Cup with a game to spare. Despite having secured their place, the player stressed that the team still has goals to achieve in the group stage. “I’m very happy. Thank God we managed to qualify after our second game, but we still have one last match. We’re preparing for that game so we can finish top of the group,” he said. The forward also noted that the standard of the competition demands focus and commitment in every match. In his view, the national team must keep their feet on the ground and keep working to achieve their ultimate goal. “Every game will be a final. There won’t be any easy games for us. That’s why we have to keep working, with our feet firmly on the ground, to reach our ultimate goal,” he added. With two wins in two games, Brazil reached six points and secured qualification with a match to spare. The national team wraps up its group-stage campaign against Costa Rica on Friday (27), seeking another positive result to finish top of Group I. item.title: 5 Real Madrid stars ‘looking out for’ Vinícius Jr. amid difficult recent spell
item.description: 5 Real Madrid stars ‘looking out for’ Vinícius Jr. amid difficult recent spell A quintet of Real Madrid stars have done their best to rally behind teammate Vinícius Jr, amid the Brazilian’s struggles across the season to date. Wide-man Vinícius is for his part of course fresh off a much-needed bounce-back performance over the weekend, when the 26-year-old emerged from the bench to change the game en route to a comeback victory for Real Madrid over Celta Vigo. Prior to as much, though, for a number of weeks, Vinícius had been the subject of widespread criticism for the level of his performances. The pressure of this backlash had a visible toll on the attacker, who at times looked completely bereft of confidence on the pitch. As alluded to above, though, all the while, a group of fellow members of José Mourinho’s squad did their utmost to keep his spirits high. As per a report from The Athletic : ‘In the dressing room, Madrid captain Federico Valverde, Eduardo Camavinga, Jude Bellingham and compatriots Eder Militao and Endrick are among the team-mates who are looking out for him the most.’ Conor Laird – GSFN

item.title: Rilany Silva calls up 30 for Brazil women’s U17 training at Granja Comary
item.description: Rilany Silva calls up 30 for Brazil women’s U17 training at Granja Comary Rilany Silva, head coach of Brazil’s U-17 Women’s National Team, has called up 30 players for an assessment and training camp from December 8 to 15 at Granja Comary in Teresópolis. The camp will take place one month after the U-17 World Cup, held in Morocco. Brazil finished fourth for the second time in the competition’s history. This is the final squad announcement of the year, with a focus on the next cycle. The list includes players who represented the U-17 national team at the 2026 South American Championship and World Cup and will still be eligible for the age group next year, but most of the squad is new. These players have not yet worked with coach Rilany Silva but are now old enough to join the team. Some have already trained and competed with the U-15s. “This call-up will help us identify the types of players who can strengthen the group staying on at U-17 level, who already have World Cup and continental tournament experience. I know what qualities we need and the standards required for them to be competitive, especially at the World Cup. The goal is to build on our work toward the South American Championship and the World Cup with those who have already experienced these tournaments,” Rilany said. item.description: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - NOVEMBER 08: Former New England Patriots tight end Rob Gronkowski looks on during halftime against the Green Bay Packers at Gillette Stadium on November 08, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Maddie Meyer/Getty Images) Getty The New England Patriots have many names left in the race for Canton. Rob Gronkowski, Vince Wilfork, Rodney Harrison and Logan Mankins advanced in voting for the Pro Football Hall of Fame’s Class of 2027. The four franchise standouts headline a group of nine former Patriots still under consideration. The Hall announced Nov. 24 that 52 players remain. The Selection Committee will next trim that field to 25 nominees. Patriots On SI’s Ethan Hurwitz identified the nine players with Patriots ties: Gronkowski, Wilfork, Rodney Harrison, Mankins, Fred Taylor, Antonio Brown, Reggie Wayne, Torry Holt and James Harrison. (Photo by Billie Weiss/Getty Images) Getty FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - NOVEMBER 08: Former New England Patriots tight end Rob Gronkowski looks on during halftime against the Green Bay Packers at Gillette Stadium on November 08, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. The Pro Football Hall of Fame announced that nine former Patriots advanced in voting for the Class of 2027: • RB Fred Taylor• WR Antonio Brown• WR Reggie Wayne• WR Torry Holt• TE Rob Gronkowski• OG Logan Mankins• DT Vince Wilfork• LB James Harrison• S Rodney… — Ethan Hurwitz (@HurwitzSports) November 24, 2026 Their New England resumes vary widely. Some helped define the franchise’s championship years. Others made brief stops, including two receivers who never reached the regular season with the team. Rob Gronkowski Advances in First Year of Hall of Fame Eligibility Getty FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS – NOVEMBER 08: Former New England Patriots tight end Rob Gronkowski looks on during halftime against the Green Bay Packers at Gillette Stadium on November 08, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Billie Weiss/Getty Images) Gronkowski enters this voting cycle with a career that won’t only be measured by his highlight catches. He earned five Pro Bowl selections and four Associated Press first-team All-Pro honors. He won three Super Bowls with New England before adding a fourth championship with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . According to his Patriots Hall of Fame biography , Gronkowski caught 521 passes for 7,861 yards and 79 touchdowns during nine regular seasons in New England. He added 81 receptions for 1,163 yards and 12 touchdowns in the postseason with the Patriots. His 2011 season is a high point of his case. Gronkowski caught 17 touchdown passes that year, setting the NFL single-season record for a tight end. New England honored him with induction into its own Hall of Fame this month. Canton would add recognition of his full NFL career. That outcome still requires several rounds of voting. Vince Wilfork, Rodney Harrison and Logan Mankins Remain in Contention Getty FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS – SEPTEMBER 25: Former New England Patriots player Vince Wilfork celebrates during his Patriots Hall of Fame induction ceremony at Gillette Stadium on September 25, 2022 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Maddie Meyer/Getty Images) Wilfork, Harrison and Mankins give Patriots fans three more cases to follow. Wilfork spent 11 seasons in New England and helped win two Super Bowls. His team Hall of Fame biography credits him with five Pro Bowl selections and four AP All-Pro honors, including first-team recognition in 2012. Harrison also won two championships with the Patriots. He finished his NFL career with 30.5 sacks and 34 interceptions, a rare combination that underscores his impact against both the run and pass. Mankins earned six Pro Bowl selections with New England and a seventh with Tampa Bay. The Patriots’ account of his career notes that he started all 130 regular-season games and 17 postseason games in which he appeared for the team. The broader nine-player count includes Holt and Wayne, whose Patriots tenures ended before they played a regular-season game for New England. There’s another Patriots connection aside from the player field. Bill Belichick and Robert Kraft have advanced as the coach and contributor candidates. The Hall’s updated process will place them alongside 13 player candidates at the annual selection meeting. Curious observers can only wait and see who will make it in. item.title: Eric Bieniemy Sets The Line For Emmett Johnson
item.description: Denny Medley-Imagn Images Chiefs offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy made his stance clear on Tuesday regarding the backfield plan. He stated that Kenneth Walker is the starter and will stay the starter once he returns to the lineup. This comment came after rookie Emmett Johnson posted strong numbers while Walker recovered from a groin injury. The team scored 34 points against the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday, a game where Johnson carried the load. Bieniemy spoke to reporters after the win and was blunt about the hierarchy. “Well, first of all, Kenneth (Walker) is the starter, and if Kenneth is playing, he’ll remain the starter,” said Bieniemy. He added that the team has been happy to watch Johnson step up during the absence. “That’s how this deal rolls. It’s been great having an opportunity to watch Emmett (Johnson) do his thing because that’s what he’s supposed to do,” he said. The Rookie’s Hot Streak Three of his last four games since Week 8 yielded over 140 scrimmage yards. That span of 491 scrimmage yards places him fourth in the league. No other rookie has accumulated more total scrimmage yards this season than him. During Sunday’s victory against Arizona, Johnson found the end zone for the fifth time on a three-yard run. He ran the ball 23 times for 105 yards and caught four passes for 38 additional yards. During the last two weeks alone, Johnson gained 206 rushing yards and 108 yards on 10 catches. He has scored a touchdown in four consecutive games. Chiefs Wire reported that these stats indicate he is ready for the next challenge. A Bigger Test Awaits Thursday night brings a harder challenge for the Chiefs as they visit the Buffalo Bills. While the Bills’ stout defense aims to halt Johnson’s momentum, his current form indicates he can withstand the pressure. “I thought offensively that we probably, in my opinion, played our most complete game to date, which was good,” Bieniemy said. He noted that the team still has things to clean up before facing Buffalo. Bieniemy also praised the value of having a healthy Walker in the mix. “We’re coaching that next man to be prepared to be the man. Emmett has done a great job, but we also understand the value that Kenneth brings as well,” he said.

item.title: Sixers Need Cisse Before Trade Deadline Hits
item.description: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images The Philadelphia 76ers have a gaping hole behind Joel Embiid that needs filling right now. A huge blow to the roster came when Ariel Hukporti tore his Achilles tendon in a preseason game. This injury left the team with Adem Bona as the primary backup, but that depth is thin. Dallas Mavericks center Moussa Cisse has emerged as a potential trade target to help fill this void. NBA insider Marc Stein identified the 76ers as one of the teams that could use a backup center, according to Sports Illustrated . The Lakers and Knicks were also listed as contenders in need of frontcourt depth. Why Dallas Might Move Cisse The Mavericks face a tricky roster math problem that could force their hand. Rookie guard Walter Clayton Jr. has been a boost off the bench and played 16 games on a two-way contract. Clayton needs a standard contract spot, but Dallas already has 15 players signed to standard deals. Someone has to go to make room for the young guard. The easiest salary to move is Cisse, who has barely played for the Mavs this season. Dallas kept Cisse over veteran Dwight Powell earlier in the year due to his age and potential. A Risky but Cheap Fix Buying Cisse makes sense on paper but carries real risk for Philadelphia. Last season, the 24-year-old who is 6-foot-11 tall recorded 14.7 points, 13.1 rebounds, and 2.1 blocks across 15 starts for the Texas Legends. His length and shot-blocking ability address the specific need for an interior presence. Yet, he remains largely unproven against NBA competition. Dusty May, the Mavericks coach, frequently employed deep rotations even though Stein observed Cisse played just 36 minutes this season. Consequently, he represents a developmental pickup instead of an instant substitute for Embiid. The Sixers cannot expect him to carry the load right away. There is a specific date when a deal can actually happen. NBA standard offseason signing rules allow Cisse to be traded starting Dec. 15. The Mavericks also matched New York’s two-year, $4.7 million offer sheet in July, which adds a layer of complexity.

item.title: DK Metcalf, Deebo Samuel, and 6 Other Must-Sit Wide Receivers in Week 12 Fantasy Football
item.description: Nov 22, 2026; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA; Philadelphia Eagles cornerback Cooper DeJean (33) is separated from Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver Dk Metcalf (4) during the third quarter at Lincoln Financial Field. Mandatory Credit: Eric Hartline-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Just as fantasy managers have to make the right start decisions, they must also make the right benching decisions. I identified the following eight wide receivers as being started in at least 15% of leagues. You need to keep them sidelined, as they offer undesirable upside in Week 12. DK Metcalf The Metcalf woes continue into Week 11. He wasn't suspended, but I cannot imagine he is a favorite of the coaching staff right now. Not to mention, the Steelers just returned Roman Wilson and hope to return Michael Pittman Jr. in Week 12. Metcalf cannot be trusted. Malik Washington Washington has three or fewer targets in three of his last five games. He has reached 50 yards just once in his last six games. The Jets rank 12th in yards per target allowed to slot wide receivers, and when the two teams met earlier this season, Washington caught only 3 passes for 27 yards, despite the offense scoring 28 points. Elic Ayomanor Hype built around a Week 10 breakout for Ayomanor. But he stumbled, and now we know why. The reason for optimism stemmed from Wan'Dale Robinson's trip to the injured reserve. Chimere Dike replaced him, catching 6 receptions on 7 targets. Deebo Samuel Samuel had just a 65% route rate in Week 11 with an average target depth of -3.7 yards. Yes, in the negative... that is correct. I think the 49ers have too many weapons to support, which limits Samuel's ceiling. Especially given that the Seahawks are the opposition, coming off a bye and widely regarded as the NFL's best defense. Khalil Shakir First, Josh Allen is quietly struggling through the air this season. He is tied for 6th-worst in interceptions and 5th-worst among currently starting quarterbacks. Shakir has just one touchdown all season, and he faces the Chiefs, who allow the 2nd-fewest fantasy points to wide receivers. Germie Bernard His time as a favorite is over. Bernard is quickly falling back to the WR4 on this team behind Metcalf, Pittman Jr., and Wilson. He caught six passes for 40 yards in Week 11, but that was his best-case scenario. My preliminary projections place Bernard outside of the top-60 wide receivers in Week 12. Keenan Allen The Seahawks allow the fewest yards per target to wide receivers. Allen ranks just 47th in PFF Receiving Grade and 85th in EPA per Target. He had 3 receptions for 38 yards in Week 11. As good as San Francisco is, Allen's upside is limited by the number of mouths that must be fed. The X post above shows that M
item.content:encoded: Nov 22, 2026; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA; Philadelphia Eagles cornerback Cooper DeJean (33) is separated from Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver Dk Metcalf (4) during the third quarter at Lincoln Financial Field. Mandatory Credit: Eric Hartline-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Just as fantasy managers have to make the right start decisions, they must also make the right benching decisions. I identified the following eight wide receivers as being started in at least 15% of leagues. You need to keep them sidelined, as they offer undesirable upside in Week 12. DK Metcalf The Metcalf woes continue into Week 11. He wasn't suspended, but I cannot imagine he is a favorite of the coaching staff right now. Not to mention, the Steelers just returned Roman Wilson and hope to return Michael Pittman Jr. in Week 12. Metcalf cannot be trusted. Malik Washington Washington has three or fewer targets in three of his last five games. He has reached 50 yards just once in his last six games. The Jets rank 12th in yards per target allowed to slot wide receivers, and when the two teams met earlier this season, Washington caught only 3 passes for 27 yards, despite the offense scoring 28 points. Elic Ayomanor Hype built around a Week 10 breakout for Ayomanor. But he stumbled, and now we know why. The reason for optimism stemmed from Wan'Dale Robinson's trip to the injured reserve. Chimere Dike replaced him, catching 6 receptions on 7 targets. Deebo Samuel Samuel had just a 65% route rate in Week 11 with an average target depth of -3.7 yards. Yes, in the negative... that is correct. I think the 49ers have too many weapons to support, which limits Samuel's ceiling. Especially given that the Seahawks are the opposition, coming off a bye and widely regarded as the NFL's best defense. Khalil Shakir First, Josh Allen is quietly struggling through the air this season. He is tied for 6th-worst in interceptions and 5th-worst among currently starting quarterbacks. Shakir has just one touchdown all season, and he faces the Chiefs, who allow the 2nd-fewest fantasy points to wide receivers. Germie Bernard His time as a favorite is over. Bernard is quickly falling back to the WR4 on this team behind Metcalf, Pittman Jr., and Wilson. He caught six passes for 40 yards in Week 11, but that was his best-case scenario. My preliminary projections place Bernard outside of the top-60 wide receivers in Week 12. Keenan Allen The Seahawks allow the fewest yards per target to wide receivers. Allen ranks just 47th in PFF Receiving Grade and 85th in EPA per Target. He had 3 receptions for 38 yards in Week 11. As good as San Francisco is, Allen's upside is limited by the number of mouths that must be fed. Chris Godwin The NFL teams who are getting "betrayed" the most this season pic.twitter.com/cPpSeN1ROk - SportsBall (@_SportsBall_) November 21, 2026 Baker Mayfield is proving to be a scam right now, given his contract compared with his level of play. The X post above shows that Mayfield is providing the least value to his team. The only viable pass-catcher that the Buccaneers have to offer is Emeka Egbuka. Godwin has 7 targets, 5 receptions, and 29 yards over his last three games. item.title: Quinyon Mitchell Injury Prediction Delivers Promising News For Eagles
item.description: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - JANUARY 11: Quinyon Mitchell #27 of the Philadelphia Eagles reacts after an interception against the San Francisco 49ers during the third quarter in the NFC Wild Card Playoff game at Lincoln Financial Field on January 11, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) Getty PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - NOVEMBER 22: Dk Metcalf #4 of the Pittsburgh Steelers cannot make the catch against Quinyon Mitchell #27 of the Philadelphia Eagles in the third quarter at Lincoln Financial Field on November 22, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. The Eagles defeated the Steelers 19-16. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) Getty Quinyon Mitchell has been ruled out for the Eagles in Week 11 with a hamstring injury Getty The Philadelphia Eagles’ defense has been thriving as of late. A lot of their success has come from the stellar secondary play headlined by the young cornerback Quinyon Mitchell. For the most part, Mitchell has avoided setbacks this season, but he had a scare during Sunday’s action against the Pittsburgh Steelers. The Eagles lost Mitchell during the second half due to a hamstring injury. As they prepare to face the Dallas Cowboys during a short week, Eagles defensive coordinator Vic Fangio seems to believe that Mitchell will be in good shape. Vic Fangio Reveals The State of Quinyon Mitchell Getty PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA – NOVEMBER 22: Dk Metcalf #4 of the Pittsburgh Steelers cannot make the catch against Quinyon Mitchell #27 of the Philadelphia Eagles in the third quarter at Lincoln Financial Field on November 22, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. The Eagles defeated the Steelers 19-16. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) Addressing reporters on Tuesday, November 24, Fangio was asked about Mitchell’s availability for Thursday’s action. It’s too early for the Eagles to put a label on his status right now, but Fangio told reporters, “I think he’ll be fine.” That’s obviously a great sign for the Eagles, who need all the help they can get against a high-powered Cowboys offense. Quinyon Mitchell’s This Season Getty Quinyon Mitchell has been ruled out for the Eagles in Week 11 with a hamstring injury In 10 games with the Eagles, Mitchell has racked up 41 tackles (32 solo). Two of his tackles were for a loss. In the passing game, Mitchell snatched one interception and deflected 11 passes. It’s been sort a quiet year for Mitchell, which is a great sign. He’s been able to lock up his opponents frequently, preventing throws from coming his way. The Eagles aren’t ready to put an official status on Mitchell just yet, but all signs have been pointing towards him getting the nod to play. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Quinyon Mitchell Injury Prediction Delivers Promising News For Eagles appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: Veteran quarterback among Tigers to know for Alabama vs. Auburn
item.description: Entering the final week of the regular season, only one team stands between Alabama and a College Football Playoff berth, the Auburn Tigers. One of college football's greatest rivalries, the Iron Bowl has a lengthy history that dates back to the late 1800's, and is a matchup which Alabama has owned in recent years. The Crimson Tide have won the last six games between the two since 2020, as well as the last three played in Tuscaloosa. This latest Iron Bowl matchup will be Kalen DeBoer's third since arriving in Tuscaloosa, with Alabama's roster led by a number of players who have seen action against the Tigers before such as Ryan Coleman-Williams, Zabien Brown, and Bray Hubbard, among others. Auburn's roster though is a mixture of players which Alabama faced a year ago, as well as numerous new faces at a few key positions. Many of these came from USF where they followed head coach Alex Golesh to Auburn this past offseason, a nonconference team that Alabama has faced twice in recent years. Here are five Tigers to know ahead of the Saturday's Iron Bowl , as well as how each has performed against Alabama before. Byrum Brown, Quarterback The USF transfer is in his first season as Auburn's starting quarterback completing 65.6% of passes for 2,035 yards and a 15:8 TD:INT ratio, while also leading the Tigers in rushing with 644 yards and nine scores on 177 attempts. As a result of his time at USF, the fifth-year senior has faced Alabama twice before in 2023-24 completing a combined 29-of-63 (46%) passes for 190 yards and one interception. Brown also rushed for 200 yards on 46 attempts during those two prior matchups. Keshaun Singleton, Wide Receiver Singleton is another USF transfer who currently leads Auburn in receiving this season with 58 catches for 744 yards and eight touchdowns. The senior did not record any stats against the Crimson Tide in 2024 while at USF. Chas Nimrod, Wide Receiver Nimrod is yet another USF transfer who sits just behind Singleton in receiving this season with 51 receptions for 638 yards and seven touchdowns. The fifth-year senior has faced Alabama twice before while at Tennessee in 2023-24, but did not record any stats in either game. Elijah Melendez, Linebacker The arguable leader of Auburn's defense is Melendez, a sophomore linebacker who leads the team with 74 tackles, 49 of which have been solo. Melendez also has 10 TFL, four sacks, one interception, and six pass defenses so far this season, and will be facing Alabama for the second time after recording one tackle a year ago in Auburn. Jeremiah Cobb, Running Back Auburn's top running back is Cobb, a senior who has 101 carries for 566 yards and four touchdowns this season, as well as 16 receptions for 141 yards and another score. This will be the running back's fourth-career meeting against Alabama, with Cobb having rushed for 33 yards and a touchdown on 10 carries a year ago. item.title: Bloodied but unbowed: Galatasaray's Gul stuns Villa
item.description: Galatasaray's Deniz Gul was covered in blood after scoring against Aston Villa (Ozan KOSE) Galatasaray inflicted Aston Villa's second successive Champions League defeat as blood-soaked Deniz Gul sealed a 1-0 victory in Istanbul on Tuesday. Gul was left with blood pouring from his face after being kicked in the head by Villa's Nicolas Jackson while the Galatasaray forward was in the process of nodding in the second-half winner at RAMS Park. Villa were unable to respond to Gul's late goal, leaving them without a victory in their last six games in all competitions. Villa won their first three league phase matches but defeats at Barcelona and now Galatasaray have derailed their bid to qualify for the last-16 via a top-eight finish. Unai Emery's side are still firmly in contention for a play-off round berth but the Spaniard will be concerned by Villa's recent dip. "To play against Galatasaray we know is very difficult. They are playing with their supporters pushing so much," Emery said. "The pitch was not helping. The match was difficult because they were pressing intensely. "We know we are not favourites to be in the top eight and of course losing today we have less chances to be there, but I am still being positive." Villa were back in Istanbul for the first time since beating Freiburg in the Europa League final in May to end their 30-year trophy drought. But those fond memories were no comfort on a dispiriting evening in Turkey. Concerns about the state of their pitch forced Galatasaray to move Saturday's home fixture against Samsunspor, while Villa were not allowed to train on the surface on Monday. Emery had admitted the patchy pitch, scarred with sand patches, was "not perfect" but warned his players not to use it as an excuse. In the end, they had only themselves to blame for a lethargic display. Galatasaray beat Liverpool twice in Istanbul in the Champions League last season. Their latest success against Premier League opposition made it three wins from five Champions League games this term. Playing to a soundtrack of ear-splitting whistles from Galatasaray fans when they touched the ball, Villa found themselves dragged into a war of attrition. Jackson has three Champions League goals already this season and the Villa striker tried to add to that tally in the opening minutes with a long-range drive that flashed wide. That was a rare sight of goal for Villa in a frenetic first half that was high on perspiration but low on inspiration. Galatasaray were without injured forwards Victor Osimhen and Rafael Leao, leaving them desperately short of cutting edge. Neither team mustered a shot on target in the first half and the second period was equally disjointed. Emery sent on Leon Goretzka and Ibrahim Mbaye for Joao Gomes and Alysson in a bid to spark Villa. They are playing with their supporters pushing so much," Emery said. "The pitch was not helping. The match was difficult because they were pressing intensely. "We know we are not favourites to be in the top eight and of course losing today we have less chances to be there, but I am still being positive." In the end, they had only themselves to blame for a lethargic display. Galatasaray beat Liverpool twice in Istanbul in the Champions League last season. Playing to a soundtrack of ear-splitting whistles from Galatasaray fans when they touched the ball, Villa found themselves dragged into a war of attrition. That was a rare sight of goal for Villa in a frenetic first half that was high on perspiration but low on inspiration. Neither team mustered a shot on target in the first half and the second period was equally disjointed. Emery sent on Leon Goretzka and Ibrahim Mbaye for Joao Gomes and Alysson in a bid to spark Villa. The move failed to pay off and Galatasaray finally broke the deadlock in the 77th minute with the first effort on target in the entire game. Emery's men failed to clear a corner and Gul survived a kick in the head from Jackson to bravely nod home from close range via a deflection off Villa defender Tyrone Mings. Gul needed a bandage applied to his wounded face but it was Villa whose European ambitions were left battered and bruised. smg/nf

item.title: Gul swoops late for buoyant Galatasaray to condemn Aston Villa to Champions League loss
item.description: This was Aston Villa’s third trip to Istanbul in the calendar year but, this time, they departed with contrasting emotions. Unlike on the banks of the Bosphorus at Besiktas Park in May, scene of their unforgettable Europa League triumph , or at Fenerbahce in January, they came away with a bloody nose. Galatasaray’s matchwinner, Deniz Gul, came away with worse than that, needing treatment after taking a boot to the face from Nicolas Jackson as he scored from a corner on 77min, the game’s first effort on target. Galatasaray maintained their commanding home form to extend Villa’s winless run to six in all competitions. A livid Unai Emery was booked for protesting to match officials as a low-quality game on a poor pitch ticked past five minutes of stoppage time. Continue reading...

item.title: Manchester United win appeal over Yoro’s red card despite Webb backing decision
item.description: Player now eligible to face Brentford on Saturday Referees’ chief Webb said it was ‘certainly not clearly wrong’ Manchester United have successfully appealed against Leny Yoro’s red card in their 4-0 defeat to Liverpool on the day referees’ chief Howard Webb gave his backing to the original decision. The defender was dismissed for denying an obvious goalscoring opportunity (Dogso) after eight minutes, but this was found to be incorrect. The Frenchman will no longer be required to serve a one-match suspension after a ruling by an independent panel. He fouled Alexander Isak when the Liverpool forward was through on goal in the early stages at Anfield but Mauricio Pochettino, United’s new head coach, insisted the striker would not have reached the ball, and therefore was not a sending-off offence. The referee Sam Barrott made a different assessment, for which the video assistant referee did not seek a review, a judgment supported by Pro Ref’s chief refereeing officer, Webb. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | The game’s gone: has fantasy football been ruined by AI gafferbots?
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Sometimes, the beautiful game can make Football Daily feel old. Even Monday’s ostensibly old-school fixture between Brentford and Everton felt like the future destroying the past. The analytics-coded hosts prevailed 4-0 and James Tarkowski was dismissed by the VAR overlords for a challenge that would have been considered “firm but fair” on the muddy pitches of our youth. “I don’t think you can tackle like that in this day and age,” a misty-eyed David Moyes sighed after the game, before heading to the team bus to rewatch the Battle of Santiago . If Sunday was Gary Neville’s Sistine Chapel [ Monday’s Football Daily ], then his commentary on the Fernando Torres goal for Chelsea against Barcelona must be his David ” – Ronnie McMahon. Regarding Declan Hackett’s assertion [ Monday’s letters ] that Donald Trump will be helping his mate Mauricio Pochettino by ringing the FA to overturn Lenny Yoro’s red card, perhaps Poch should be careful what he wishes for: Trump may equally decide to get Michael Carrick reinstated, as he also has a bit of previous for that sort of thing” – Dexter O Riordan. In all the time that I have been watching football, I don’t think I have ever seen a player dismiss himself and be away down the tunnel before given a red card. Thanks James Tarkowski ” – Nigel Sanders. Brighton had only failed to win twice in the league since 5 September. A 1-1 draw with Leeds and a 2-0 defeat at Liverpool - their only opponents with double letters in their name. That bizarre hoodoo struck again at Hull on Sunday. Good good news for Seagulls fans is the only double-lettered encounters they have before hosting Hull in February are trips to Forest and Spurs. Even better news is that since that 1-1 draw with Leeds on 5 September, they have a 100% win record against sides without double letters and have not conceded a goal” – Dan Ashley (and no others). Continue reading...

item.description: South American tournament was in US in 2024 and 2016 Concacaf teams determined by 2027 Gold Cup Games will overlap with Euro 2028 but not Olympics The 2028 Copa América will be played in the United States and expanded to include teams from the Concacaf region, bringing the landmark South American international competition to the US for a third time in five editions. Conmebol, the South American confederation that runs the tournament, and Concacaf, the confederation governing soccer in North and Central America and the Caribbean, jointly announced the long-rumored arrangement on Tuesday, framing it as an extension of a “strategic partnership” between the organizations. item.title: Senegal restored as Africa Cup of Nations champions after court ruling
item.description: Senegal won January’s final 1-0 after walking off Result was overturned in March as 3-0 win for Morocco Senegal have been reinstated as the champions of Africa, and their controversial 1-0 victory against Morocco confirmed in the record books, after the scandal over January’s Africa Cup of Nations final was resolved in a Swiss courtroom. The court of arbitration for sport (Cas) ruled that a decision to award the 2025 Afcon title to Morocco on appeal should be set aside. Senegal celebrated with a social media post proclaiming the team to have won the title twice: first on the field and then at Cas. Morocco, who are due to co-host the World Cup in 2030, declared their intention to “pursue all legal avenues” to challenge the ruling. Continue reading...

item.title: ‘I’m loving it at Brugge’: Freddie Potts on going from West Ham’s bench to Champions League
item.description: Midfielder is preparing to face Liverpool after leaving the club he loves and overcoming a tough start in Belgium In April Freddie Potts was absorbing the disappointment of being substituted at half-time during West Ham’s FA Cup quarter-final defeat by Leeds. The midfielder was out of favour under Nuno Espírito Santo and could not have imagined that he would be preparing to face Liverpool in the Champions League seven months later. It is the 23-year-old’s reward for taking the difficult decision to leave his boyhood club last summer. Potts noticed his minutes were drying up in pre-season, even though West Ham were not exactly stocked with talent after relegation, and he was ready for a new challenge when Club Brugge offered about £10m to sign him. Continue reading...

item.title: Nwaneri at risk of becoming Arsenal’s forgotten teenager on return with Dortmund
item.description: Youngest player to appear in Premier League is struggling to establish himself on loan at the Bundesliga club Ethan Nwaneri has one record Max Dowman can never break. It is more than four years since he became the youngest player to appear in the Premier League , with Dowman, his fellow Hale End academy graduate, older by 54 days when he made his highly anticipated debut . But after a week when Arsenal published an article dedicated to Dowman’s growing collection of milestones, Nwaneri risks becoming the club’s forgotten teenager. Nwaneri joined Borussia Dortmund on loan in the summer and returns to the Emirates Stadium in the Champions League on Tuesday, although the 19-year-old will probably be on the bench, having not started for the German club yet in the competition. Despite making a good impression with an assist on his Bundesliga debut, against Hoffenheim, he has not started in the league since 17 October and has yet to complete more than 65 minutes in a Bundesliga match. Continue reading...

item.title: De Bruyne’s Napoli return will remind Manchester City what they are missing
item.description: Even without the charges, the Belgian maestro will be an unwelcome throwback to happier times for Enzo Maresca As Manchester City come to terms with turbulence, one of their all-time greats has flown in to remind them of the best of times. Kevin De Bruyne will be back at the Etihad Stadium on Tuesday, evoking the greatest period of Pep Guardiola’s decade in charge when they won four straight Premier League titles and the Champions League . In Europe, things are comfortable for Enzo Maresca, with three wins from four, but they have collected a solitary point from 12 domestically recently. They are struggling to score and conceding too easily at the back, leading the Italian to experiment in his attempts to find solutions. Continue reading...

item.title: Lewis-Potter double and Janelt stunner ease Brentford past 10-man Everton
item.description: It was a record-breaking occasion in more ways than one. David Moyes made history for Everton, edging clear of Harry Catterick by overseeing his 593rd game in charge of the club, but calamitous defending ruined the Scot’s evening and defeat to Brentford was inevitable after James Tarkowski received his first red card in 351 Premier League appearances. Those in Tarkowski’s corner will claim the Everton captain’s tackle on Yehor Yarmoliuk would not have been a foul back in the day. This, though, was not a “game’s gone” moment. Not that sort of player? The reality is Tarkowski’s back catalogue features plenty of orange card tackles, meaning there was always likely to come a time when his luck ran out. Continue reading...

item.title: Madness erupts as Sevilla deny Betis in wild end to Spain’s ‘derby of derbies’
item.description: Rivals have been heading in opposite directions in recent years but latest clash showed some things never change “If we didn’t celebrate a goal, especially in this game, that would be madness,” Kike Salas said. Instead, this was madness, the kind of moment a derby is meant to have, even if it has nothing else. It was late, it was lucky, and there wasn’t even a winner but right there, right then, at 24 minutes past 8pm on Saturday evening in the Ramón Sánchez-Pizjuán Stadium, it felt like there was. Frankly it was a bit rubbish, as bad a goal as you’ll see, but it was also the best, practically Pelé against the Nazis . Suddenly there were arms and legs everywhere, tears too. Cameras confirmed it. Zoom in and there they are: actual, real life tears. In the 91st minute of the 146th meeting between Sevilla Fútbol Club and Real Betis Balompié – “derby of derbies” according to Luis García, the Sevilla coach for whom it was the first – Salas’s shot from 18 yards went through Marc Bartra’s legs and Álvaro Valles’s hands. The ball dribbled into the Betis net so apologetically it barely touched the net at all and hadn’t got there before Sevilla’s vice-captain was gone. Raised in Morón de la Frontera, to the south of a city divided , Salas joined Sevilla at 11; now, having levelled the game at 1-1, he went tearing towards the terraces, absolutely losing it like they were. Continue reading...

item.title: Mauricio Pochettino can now see just how desperate Manchester United are | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The manager’s first game in charge was a disaster and he needs to lift the mood within a sunken squad if a relegation battle is to be avoided Sign up for our free newsletter here In as much as any derby can ever be a free hit, there was always a sense that Mauricio Pochettino’s first game as Manchester United manager wouldn’t matter too much; nobody expected them to win away to Liverpool. This was not a game on which anybody was going to judge him, and that feeling only magnified when Leny Yoro was sent off after eight minutes. United’s victory at Anfield last season was their first for a decade; what’s difficult to do with 11 men is only going to get harder playing a man down for 82 minutes. But that does not mean that it did not matter. Although Roy Keane was determined to reject the suggestion, there was perhaps even some credit to be gleaned from having lost only 4-0 . Certainly when they were 2-0 down after 13 minutes, there was reason for United to fear an embarrassment akin to their 7-0 defeat against Liverpool in 2023 . Perhaps Pochettino deserves credit for his switch to a back three, which brought a degree of stabilisation, but United could easily have lost far more comfortably than they did. Liverpool had 18 shots in the game three-and-a-half years ago, eight of them on target; on Sunday they had 28, 11 of them on target. When you’ve conceded an xG of 4.38, there’s not much point quibbling over the details; you’ve been hammered. Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Wilson
item.content:encoded: The manager’s first game in charge was a disaster and he needs to lift the mood within a sunken squad if a relegation battle is to be avoided Sign up for our free newsletter here In as much as any derby can ever be a free hit, there was always a sense that Mauricio Pochettino’s first game as Manchester United manager wouldn’t matter too much; nobody expected them to win away to Liverpool. This was not a game on which anybody was going to judge him, and that feeling only magnified when Leny Yoro was sent off after eight minutes. United’s victory at Anfield last season was their first for a decade; what’s difficult to do with 11 men is only going to get harder playing a man down for 82 minutes. But that does not mean that it did not matter. Although Roy Keane was determined to reject the suggestion, there was perhaps even some credit to be gleaned from having lost only 4-0 . Certainly when they were 2-0 down after 13 minutes, there was reason for United to fear an embarrassment akin to their 7-0 defeat against Liverpool in 2023 . Perhaps Pochettino deserves credit for his switch to a back three, which brought a degree of stabilisation, but United could easily have lost far more comfortably than they did. Liverpool had 18 shots in the game three-and-a-half years ago, eight of them on target; on Sunday they had 28, 11 of them on target. When you’ve conceded an xG of 4.38, there’s not much point quibbling over the details; you’ve been hammered. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Neville, Keane and Manchester United meltdowns at world’s funniest comedy club
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Hoo-boy. Short of forgetting to put on his washable virgin wool navy trousers before striding towards the visitors’ dugout at Anfield, it’s difficult to imagine how Mauricio Pochettino’s spell in charge of Manchester United could have got off to a more humiliating start. Having witnessed his new team go a man and two goals down in less time than it takes to listen to Led Zeppelin’s Stairway to Heaven twice, it was a rendition of Sacked In The Morning that could be heard from the home fans inside 15 minutes. Poch would later complain that the decision to dismiss Leny Yoro was questionable, but it was far less baffling than his own call to hand Matthijs de Ligt his first Premier League start in a year after almost 12 months out with knack. Across 90 harrowing minutes, the Dutch defender didn’t so much look off the pace as resemble a confused tourist who’d wandered on to the pitch while trying to find his way to the stadium museum. In a footballing world obsessed with micro-marginal-gains – think custom-weighted laces, aerodynamic socks, or nice calming shades of green for training ground walls – how about one modest proposal that otherwise does my nut in? That a multimillion pound player, paid hundred of thousands each week, has to walk all the way around the pitch with ligament injuries . Carry him, give him crutches, or put him in a wheelchair! Is it just me? It has a very 1950s amateur air of ‘dont make a fuss, ‘tis a mere scratch’” – John Williams. Since he was such a good friend to Mauricio Pochettino in his previous role, can we assume Donald Trump will be ringing the FA to overturn Lenny Yoro’s red card once he’s finished his morning nap?” – Declan Hackett. If Mikel Arteta is correct in his assertion that “ We are not in Disneyland, we are in the Premier League ” how does he explain his team’s Micky Mouse defending for Newcastle’s second goal at St James’ Park on Sunday?” – Dominic Hodgson. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: PSG had the best attack in Europe but Doué and Kvaratskhelia injuries will test Luis Enrique
item.description: Désiré Doué sustained an ACL injury in PSG’s 3-2 win at Nice and joins Khvicha Kvaratskhelia on the treatment table By Get French Football News Luis Enrique is in uncharted territory, even if he insists that “it isn’t a first”. Since arriving at Paris Saint-Germain in 2023, only three players have spent more than 100 days on the sideline – Nuno Mendes, Lucas Hernandez and Presnel Kimpembe – and only Mendes is an important first-team player. But for the remainder of the season, or at least the vast majority of it, Luis Enrique must do without two of his stars: Désiré Doué and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia. Doué arrived in Nice on Saturday evening already bearing scars. The PSG forward wore a mouth guard after Davide Frattesi had dislodged one of his front teeth with a stray arm during France’s defeat by Italy during the international break. Continue reading...

item.title: Esposito emulates Vieri with Inter hat-trick but De Ketelaere haunts him again
item.description: Italy’s new cover star enjoyed a ‘beautiful’ treble but could not celebrate it after his side threw away two-goal leads three times to draw 4-4 with Atalanta This ought to have been a magic moment for Pio Esposito. He had just scored his first Serie A hat-trick, becoming only the third Italian to get one for Inter in the era of three points for a win. The last to do it was Christian Vieri, back in 2003. Two years before Esposito was born. We will come back to that. Esposito has been drawing premature comparisons to Vieri for some time and especially now after a barnstorming November in which he has scored eight times in five games, including three in two for his country, and two of those as part of a man-of-the-match performance during an upset win against France . Continue reading...

item.title: Jamal Musiala controversy the nadir of Bayern Munich’s turbulent week
item.description: German giants’ treatment of midfielder has raised questions about how far the reputation of a family club still holds It was, on paper, a perfect Friday evening for Bayern to flex their muscles once again, in the chill of their intimidating Allianz Arena against struggling opponents who had won just twice all season in the league. In the end, though, the best news of the night was that Saïd El Mala, the star of the visitors, Köln, who had scored a jaw-dropping consolation goal at the same stadium in spring, fluffed a far easier chance in the closing stages that would have condemned the champions to defeat. The word crisis is rampantly overused in sport, but this was the weekend Bayern’s injury troubles reached critical mass. With Luis Díaz, Serge Gnabry and Ismaël Saibari already missing, their talisman Harry Kane had his game curtailed after 20 minutes and by the time the second half had begun, they’d lost Michael Olise too. Continue reading...

item.title: Infantino’s $20bn World Cup sell-off plan was to run for up to 96 years, documents show
item.description: Management team were in line for huge payouts Fifa denies Infantino would have profited from plan Gianni Infantino’s failed Fifa Forward Enterprise plan could have locked football in for up to 96 years while paying its management up to 5% of the scheme’s multibillion-pound value, according to documents seen by the Guardian. Previously undisclosed communications by Fifa and Thrive Capital, the lead investor for the proposal, cast fresh light on the deal to sell off football’s crown jewels. They outline a plan, produced days before July’s final of the 2026 World Cup, to profit from the sport’s burgeoning commercial revenues for almost a century. Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s action
item.description: Leeds offer Chelsea a lesson, Newcastle’s summer recruits struggle and Jules Ahoka makes a name for himself What to make of Manchester United’s utterly torrid start under Mauricio Pochettino? To go glass half full as the new head coach had only three days to prepare the side for the trip to Anfield, the hope will be that time will cast the 4-0 humbling from Liverpool as the falsest of false starts. The glass-half-empty scenario, though, is that here was an XI packed with internationals that had zero clue how to sort out a dire beginning themselves. Leny Yoro’s very early red card may have been questionable but for the wall to evaporate and allow Dominik Szoboszlai’s subsequent free-kick to arrow home was damning evidence of how immature Pochettino’s new charges are. From here it became a debacle and the players, if they have anything about them, need to apologise to the head coach, hold a meeting between themselves and demand they start taking responsibility. If not, United are heading only one way: down. Jamie Jackson Match report: Liverpool 4-0 Manchester United ‘It’s painful for me’: Pochettino criticises Yoro red card decision Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Football’s political gamers face off at Fifa with the real-life final boss
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Although the millions of gamers who are pulling sickies would beg to differ, the release of Grand Theft Auto VI wasn’t the most exciting midnight launch involving a sprawling enterprise full of shady characters. Over in Zurich, the clock also struck 12 on the candidate deadline for next year’s Fifa presidential election, leaving those of us who have no interest in video games with our own chaotic, multi-billion-dollar sandbox where untouchable bosses bend the rules to suit themselves. While online carjackers are busy exploring a “most extraordinarily, indulgently detailed virtual world” , football’s real-life power brokers are gearing up for a March showdown in the actual city of Rabat. When I first saw the photo in yesterday’s Football Daily , I thought Mauricio Pochettino had opted for a short back and sides, presumably to pre-empt him tearing his luscious locks out in frustration at forthcoming poor results/terrible January transfer window/petulant sniping from sulky squad members. Then I realised he was in the back seat, all but entirely obscured by the rear-view mirror, in which he could perhaps see his sense of job satisfaction disappearing …” – Phil Taverner. That photo of Pochettino being chauffeured by a beefy driver answered one of my burning questions: what’s Ange Postecoglou doing these days?” – Mike Wilner (and others). This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: Danny Kelly loved football and never forgot the absurdity of earning a living talking about it | Max Rushden
item.description: The journalist and broadcaster who died last week aged 69 knew the enduring power of radio, even as the landscape changed so quickly It’s injury time at the Emirates on 29 October 2008, Arsenal are 4-3 up against Tottenham. Tom Huddlestone cushions a ball to Luka Modric, whose strike takes a deflection. It loops over Manuel Almunia and off a post into the path of Aaron Lennon, who prods it home and starts skipping towards the Spurs supporters before diving on to the ground and being enveloped by Modric, Benoît Assou-Ekotto, Darren Bent and a couple of pitch-invading fans. Pandemonium, for once, seems the apt way to describe it. But the real entertainment is happening in a radio studio at 18 Hatfields, London SE1; the old home of TalkSport. As the goal goes in, a guttural voice makes an indecipherable but very loud noise. It’s hard to transcribe – perhaps “ERRRRRAAAARRRGGHH”, or maybe “OOEEERRAAGGH”. It’s just a noise, but it’s unmistakably Danny Kelly. He regains the power of speech and follows it up with: “Gooooaaaal … Goalll Stan, Goalll at the Emirates.” Reporter Ian Abrahams and Stan Collymore join the excitement, before Danny comes back: “I LOVE FOOTBALL, STAN, I LOVE IT.” It is such a brilliant piece of radio . From one of the absolute greats. Continue reading...

item.title: Mauricio Pochettino’s USMNT time will be remembered fondly, but it wasn’t transformational
item.description: The incoming Manchester United manager improved the US team’s culture and competitiveness, but could not bring about sea change in two years In a theater high up in a midtown Manhattan skyscraper built from lots of glass, a highlight reel played to deafening music. And then, on “a monumental day for US Soccer”, federation president, Cindy Parlow Cone, announced they had bagged their man, Mauricio Pochettino, to become the highest-profile United States manager in the men’s national team’s history. Pochettino held court for three-quarters of an hour in his signature blend of Spanglish before the assembled media and a grab bag of sponsors. Then he recorded some TV hits. And after that, in a bit of accidental prescience, he went off to record a podcast with Gary Neville. Continue reading...

item.title: Netflix, Fox and the $2bn bid for the 2030 World Cup that could reshape live sports
item.description: The battle for the US TV rights to the tournament will pit the traditional broadcaster against the ‘whatever-it-takes’ streamer. It could be a tipping point in the industry The awarding of broadcast rights in the United States for this year’s World Cup was a cut-price deal to avoid legal action from the existing rights holders, Fox Sports. This week’s tender process for the 2030 tournament will be anything but. Media rights and broadcast experts canvassed by the Guardian in the US and Europe are united in agreement that Fifa will benefit from the most competitive and expensive auction in the competition’s history. It is expected to fetch between $1.5bn (£1.13bn) and $2bn, with some predicting the outcome could be a landmark moment for the sports and entertainment industry. Continue reading...

item.title: Swing when you’re winning? Biggest leaps across Fifa’s football rankings | The Knowledge
item.description: Plus: clubs with roads on their team badges, most and fewest managers per league title, and more Mail us with all of your questions and answers “The Scotland men’s team’s highest Fifa ranking was 13th (in 2007) and the worst was 88th place (in 2005) – a difference of 75 positions,” writes Bogdan Kotarlic. “Is this the biggest gap between the best and worst ranking for one national team?” The gap between Scotland’s best and worst Fifa rankings isn’t the biggest in men’s international football; in fact, Pete Tomlin calculates that a 75-place swing puts them joint 141st with Ghana and Seychelles. And, as Chris Lewis and others point out, there are a couple of other home nations who have had more dramatic swings. Wales and Northern Ireland both moved up 109 places: Wales from 117th to eighth under Gary Speed and then Chris Coleman, Northern Ireland from 129th in 2004 to 20th in 2017. 183 places Montenegro (16th/199th) 165 Kuwait (24/189) 160 Bosnia and Herzegovina (13/173) 155 Cape Verde (27/182) 153 Central African Republic (49/202) 151 Libya (36/187) 146 Equatorial Guinea (49/195) 144 Moldova (37/181) 141 El Salvador (49/190) 136 Cuba (46/182), Slovakia (14/150) Continue reading...

item.title: Reliving the drama: England and Argentina stars watch 1986 classic with fresh eyes
item.description: A new film about the historic World Cup quarter-final clash finds new angles for a new generation “Is there anything new to say about it?” Gary Lineker asked the producer Flora Fernandez-Marengo when she first approached him to take part in The Match, a documentary about the 1986 World Cup quarter-final between England and Argentina. Flora told an audience at the London film festival premiere of the film that she played her best card then and showed Lineker an image of Maradona with Queen in 1981, during the band’s tour of Argentina. Maradona wearing a union jack T-shirt and Freddie Mercury an Argentina strip. It worked. Lineker said yes. The rock’n’roll angle, with Brian May as a talking head, is one of the very few details the film-makers added to Andrés Burgo’s book, The Match, on which the documentary is based. The directors Juan Cabral and Santiago Franco play with the timeline, hopping between past and present across 91 minutes, the exact duration of the match itself. Anecdotes that now form part of Argentina’s football folklore are spliced with excellent archive material. Continue reading...

item.title: Janine van Wyk: ‘Our rooms were empty … no mattresses, no lightbulbs and not a drop of water’
item.description: In an extract from the former South Africa captain’s book, she details less than ideal Wafcon 2006 preparations I was just a year into my international career when we qualified for my first Wafcon, which was then called the African Women’s Championship (AWC) and was held in Nigeria in 2006. I was extremely excited but very nervous to participate in this tournament, more so when it was announced that we would be in the same group as the hosts, and would play them last in the group. As it turned out, it would be the game that decided who finished top of the group. By then we had beaten Algeria 4-0 and Equatorial Guinea 2-0 and had to travel to Delta State to take on the hosts. I’d heard that Nigeria was the toughest country to travel to and I was about to realise why. It’s become common knowledge that South Africans and Nigerians are massive rivals on the football field but also don’t really get on off it. Continue reading...

item.title: Thomas Frank’s to-do list: lift mood, fix defence and fire up Sarr and Mateta
item.description: Seeking redemption after failing at Spurs, newly installed Crystal Palace manager has a tough challenge ahead Thomas Frank promised his wife, Nanna, he would take a year’s sabbatical after being sacked by Tottenham in February , but he couldn’t wait that long. Having received a reported £8m payoff from Spurs, he kept an extremely low profile in the first few months after an experience at the club that sources close to the 53‑year‑old have described as “traumatic”. Frank broke his silence at the start of June with a statement released by the League Managers Association. It said he would cover the World Cup for the BBC (thereby going head-to-head with Ange Postecoglou, his predecessor at Spurs, who worked for ITV) before “experiencing the Tour de France”, a lifelong passion. Frank usually preferred to run to Brentford’s training ground and home matches from his home in East Sheen during a nine‑year spell as assistant and then manager, but he occasionally cycled because it helped to clear his head. Continue reading...

item.title: Echoes of Azteca but not like Argentina: fearless England start afresh in Madrid
item.description: ‘We will not go back on this way of playing,’ says Thomas Tuchel after he delivered response to World Cup critics Thomas Tuchel made defensive substitutions as England protected a lead. He finished with three centre-backs on the pitch. His team could not get out of their half in the final part of the game. So close your eyes and imagine an alternate universe in which James Trafford did not make his stunning double save in stoppage time on Sunday and England had drawn 3-3 with Spain at the Metropolitano Stadium rather than won 3-2 . The reaction would not have been kind because Tuchel has been here before. The head coach wanted to push one particular comparison from the World Cup over the summer. “It was Mexico reloaded,” he said, with a nod towards the 3-2 last-16 win at the Azteca Stadium and it fitted like a glove – down to the detail of Jarell Quansah and red cards. Continue reading...

item.title: WSL talking points: Chelsea’s gamble pays off and have Arsenal lost fear factor?
item.description: Blues beat champions after bold substitution and Gunners’ home struggles continue with fifth consecutive WSL draw Sonia Bompastor attempted to deflect suggestions that the removal of Kadeisha Buchanan 12 minutes into Chelsea’s top-of-the-table clash with Manchester City was tactical, but few were convinced by the claim that it was down to injury. The manager said the centre-back, who had not asked to come off and walked straight down the tunnel, had taken a knock to the head in training and been assessed and cleared, but that during the game “she was not herself”. On came Veerle Buurman and the threat of Khadija Shaw was nullified, the Dutch defender restricting the golden boot favourite so well that Shaw did not manage a shot on target. Bompastor said after the game that she had not spoken to Buchanan but that she would “explain myself to her”. “I always have good relationships with the players, bring them clarity, and I’m always direct and honest so they have the information,” she said. “It won’t be any different.” Enforced or not, the substitution was a huge gamble that paid off, even after the loss of Melvine Malard to injury in the first half reduced their number of remaining in-game substitution windows to one. Suzanne Wrack Match report: Chelsea 1-0 Manchester City Continue reading...

item.title: European football body’s plan to go global leaves Fifa on tenterhooks
item.description: Findings of ‘feasibility study’ into quest for world domination loom with Europe’s wealthiest certain to benefit whatever the outcome It will be one of the most eagerly devoured documents in football circles, assuming its contents are ever fully revealed. In September, the increasingly powerful European Football Clubs body announced a “feasibility study” into how it can become established on a more global scale, morphing into an organisation that represents clubs all over the world. The study’s findings could, some leading figures in the sport’s governance believe, define football’s long-term future. It has the potential to transform a landscape destabilised by the scandals surrounding Fifa and Gianni Infantino . Continue reading...
